00_vault-map/cityuhk-cs-admission-at-a-g.content:
CityUHK CS Admission at a Glance: Key Facts


                  
                  Short answer 
                  
                

Headline numbers: ~85 local CS places, best-5 weight-1 JUPAS formula, no interview, non-JUPAS ASI/ASII routes for AD/HD/IB/A-Level, and 97.5% graduate employment.


Question
What are the headline facts a parent should remember about CityUHK CS admission?
Answer


Programmes: BSc Computer Science (JS1204), BSc Cybersecurity (JS1218), the CS + Computational Finance/FinTech double degree (JS1221), and data-science programmes run by the same College of Computing.


Indicative intake (2026/27): 85 local places for JS1204 (first year + Advanced Standing I combined); 29 local places for JS1218 (first year + ASI combined).


Minimum entry (JUPAS): English 3, Chinese 3, Mathematics 3, CSD attained, plus Level 3 in one elective from Biology / Chemistry / ICT / M1/M2 / Physics, and Level 3 in a second elective.


No blanket JUPAS interview for CS or Cybersecurity - the arrangement is ‘When necessary’.


Non-JUPAS routes exist: Advanced Standing I (Year 2) and Advanced Standing II (Senior Year) for AD/HD holders, plus Year 1 entry for IB and GCE A Level candidates.


Outcome: 97.5% of BSc CS graduates were in full-time employment (Graduate Employment Survey 2024).


Examples

A student with 544AA (Eng 5, Math 4, ICT 4, plus 2 other 4s) scores 23.5 on JS1204’s best-5 formula - comfortably above the 2026 lower quartile of 22.
An associate-degree holder with CGPA 3.2 can skip the A-Level route and apply for Advanced Standing I (Year 2) in CS with code 1561A.

00_vault-map/is-cityuhk-cs-a-college-of-.content:
Is CityUHK CS a College of Computing Programme


                  
                  Short answer 
                  
                

BSc CS, BSc Cybersecurity and the Data Science programmes all sit in the College of Computing, sharing first-year requirements, one application portal, and easier cross-programme switching.


Question
What is the College of Computing and why does it matter?
Answer
BSc CS (JS1204), BSc Cybersecurity (JS1218) and the data-science programmes (JS1071/1072/1074) all sit in the College of Computing. The college groups computing, data science and business-analytics programmes, so year-1 students share college-specified courses (like calculus and linear algebra) and can sometimes switch between related programmes (e.g., from BSc Data Science to BSc Data and Systems Engineering) more easily than across colleges.
For admission, it means one application portal, one set of first-year requirements, and joint events (open days, workshops) across the family of programmes.

00_vault-map/jupas-for-cityuhk-cs-the-bi.title: JUPAS for CityUHK CS: The Big Picture
00_vault-map/jupas-for-cityuhk-cs-the-bi.content:
JUPAS for CityUHK CS: The Big Picture


                  
                  Short answer 
                  
                

JUPAS is the single application to 9 universities, including CityUHK. CS (JS1204) and Cybersecurity (JS1218) admit mainly on a weighted HKDSE score, with no blanket interview - selection is on results, OEA, Principal’s Nominations and band choice.


Question
What is JUPAS and why does it matter for getting into CityUHK CS?
Answer
JUPAS (Joint University Programmes Admissions System) is the single application through which HKDSE candidates apply to 9 participating universities, including CityUHK. For BSc Computer Science (JS1204) and BSc Cybersecurity (JS1218), JUPAS is the main local route: you list CityUHK programmes among your 10 choices and offers are made in the Main Round in early August.
CityUHK’s selection is score-driven: your HKDSE results are converted to level points, weighted by the programme’s formula, and you are ranked. For JS1204 the formula is simply the best 5 subjects at weight 1 (no extra weighting in 2026). There is no blanket interview - selection is effectively on results, OEA, Principal’s Nominations and band choice as tie-breakers.

00_vault-map/vault-freshness-and-verific.title: Vault Freshness and Verification Status
00_vault-map/vault-freshness-and-verific.content:
Vault Freshness and Verification Status


                  
                  Short answer 
                  
                

Every note is stamped retrieved: 2026-09 and status: verified (checked against official PDFs, 2023-2026 cycles) or status: draft (the proposed 1.5x policy, not yet confirmed published). Re-check any note whose retrieved date is older than your entry cycle.


Question
How up to date and reliable is the information in this vault, and how do I know what to trust?
Answer
Every note carries two lines in its frontmatter: retrieved (when the content was checked against its source) and status - either verified or draft.


verified: the content was checked against an official public document (CityUHK JUPAS formula/score PDFs, JUPAS 9-institution score files, the CS course catalogue). This covers all published score data for the 2023-2026 entry cycles, fees, dates and curriculum.


draft: the content tracks a proposed policy rather than a published one - currently only the 1.5x weighting note. The 1.5x policy is promoted by the CS admissions team but the published 2026 formula still reads best-5 weight 1, so treat draft content as ‘likely but confirm’.


How to tell if something is stale: if a note’s retrieved date is older than the entry cycle you are applying for, re-confirm its numbers against the document named in its Source line before relying on them. For the 2027 cycle, CityUHK will publish the new formula and prior-year scores around January 2027 - this vault is regenerated from those official PDFs after each JUPAS results release (mid-July).
Published admission scores are reference points, not cut-offs: they describe the middle (median) and bottom quarter (lower quartile) of admitted students in a past cycle. They are not comparable across programmes or universities.

What Does the CS Department’s Research Focus Mean for Students


                  
                  Short answer 
                  
                

The department’s research (AI, data science, security, systems, multimedia) shapes the electives and final-year project topics you can choose, and feeds MSc/PhD pathways.


Question
Does research activity at CityUHK CS matter for an undergraduate?
Answer
Yes, indirectly but importantly. The Department’s research foci - AI, bioinformatics, cloud computing, data science, evolutionary computation, information security, machine learning, mobile computing, multimedia, software engineering, vision and graphics - shape the electives and final-year project topics students work on. Students get access to a private cloud infrastructure and a high-throughput computing cluster.
In practice this means: final-year projects in e-commerce, VR, computer vision, cloud and information security; industry-linked projects through the internship; and a pipeline of MSc/PhD pathways (MSc CS, MSc AI) for those who want to continue.

01_jupas-basics/1.5x-subject-weighting-p.title: 1.5x Subject Weighting Policy (Draft) Status
01_jupas-basics/1.5x-subject-weighting-p.content:
1.5x Subject Weighting Policy (Draft) Status


                  
                  Short answer 
                  
                

Proposed policy: English, Mathematics, ICT, M1, M2, Physics, Chemistry and Biology counted at 1.5x level points. Caveat: the published 2026 JS1204 formula is still best-5 at weight 1, so the 1.5x policy may or may not be on the admission site yet - confirm the year’s official formula.




                  
                  🎓 Admission talk Q5 — the NEW 1.5x weighting policy · ⬅ back to cover page
                  
                

Question
What is the new 1.5x weighting policy for CS and is it already on the admission site?
Answer
CityUHK is emphasizing a new weighting policy under which eight discipline-related subjects are weighted at 1.5x in the JUPAS admission score: English, Mathematics, ICT, M1, M2, Physics, Chemistry, and Biology. Under this policy each of these subjects contributes 1.5 times its level points; other elective subjects stay at weight 1.
Status / important caveat: The officially published 2026 JUPAS main admission score formula for JS1204 (BSc Computer Science) on the CityUHK admission site currently reads best 5 subjects, weight 1 (no 1.5x applied), and the same for JS1218 and JS1221. The 1.5x policy is the approach the CS admissions team is promoting to applicants and may or may not be reflected in the current admission site at the time of reading. Always confirm the exact formula in the year’s ‘Admission Score Formula and Admissions Scores’ PDF before applying.
Why it matters: 1.5x strongly rewards strong results in exactly the subjects a CS student will use. A student with 5s in English, Math and ICT gains far more under 1.5x than a student with 5s in unrelated electives - so subject choice in DSE matters for CS ranking.
Worked comparison (same 5 subjects, two ways of scoring):























ScenarioSubjects (level)Weight-1 total (published 2026)1.5x total (policy)Strong science profileEng 5, Math 5, ICT 5, Physics 4, Chem 45.5+5.5+5.5+4+4 = 24.58.25+8.25+8.25+6+6 = 36.75Mixed electivesEng 5, Math 4, ICT 4, Econ 4, Hist 45.5+4+4+4+4 = 21.58.25+6+6+4+4 = 28.25
The gap between the two scenarios widens dramatically under 1.5x (12.5 points vs 3 points), which is the whole point of the policy: it differentiates applicants who actually studied the CS-relevant subjects.
Examples

If you are advising a student on DSE subject choice for CS, the 1.5x policy says: a 5 in Mathematics is worth 1.5x as much as a 5 in a non-listed elective, so prioritizing Math + ICT + one of Physics/Chem over a non-science elective improves the CS admission score under the policy.

01_jupas-basics/cityuhk-tuition-fees.title: CityUHK Tuition Fees
01_jupas-basics/cityuhk-tuition-fees.content:
CityUHK Tuition Fees


                  
                  Short answer 
                  
                

For 2026/27 entry, the local (JUPAS/Non-JUPAS local) undergraduate tuition fee at CityUHK is approximately HK$47,000 per year for the standard four-year JUPAS programmes. Non-local (international) tuition is set separately and is higher;…




                  
                  🎓 Admission talk Q10 — scholarships and cost · ⬅ back to cover page
                  
                

Question
How much does an undergraduate degree at CityUHK cost, and are CS programmes different?
Answer
For 2026/27 entry, the local (JUPAS/Non-JUPAS local) undergraduate tuition fee at CityUHK is approximately HK$47,000 per year for the standard four-year JUPAS programmes. Non-local (international) tuition is set separately and is higher; government-funded places are reserved for local students, so international applicants are admitted to non-local places at non-local fees.
JUPAS programmes (including JS1204 BSc Computer Science and JS1218 BSc Cybersecurity) all charge the standard local fee. The double degree JS1221 (BSc CS + BSc Computational Finance and Financial Technology) runs five years, so total tuition is roughly 5x the annual fee - a material difference from the four-year single degrees. Students from overseas (non-local places) pay the non-local fee for each year.
Beyond tuition, expect typical University living/study costs (student union fees, books, accommodation) which are not part of the tuition figure. CityUHK publishes a full fee schedule each cycle - confirm the exact figures for your entry year on the official degree fees page before applying, as fees are reviewed periodically.
Examples

A local JUPAS student in JS1204 pays roughly HK47,000 x 4 = HK188,000 in tuition over four years, versus roughly HK$235,000 for the five-year JS1221 double degree - the extra year is the main cost difference between the two routes.

01_jupas-basics/how-cityuhk-ranks-tied-j.title: How CityUHK Ranks Tied JUPAS Candidates
01_jupas-basics/how-cityuhk-ranks-tied-j.content:
How CityUHK Ranks Tied JUPAS Candidates


                  
                  Short answer 
                  
                

CityUHK’s published JS1204 selection criteria say that with equal scores, the university refers to: (1) results in discipline-related subjects (e.g., Mathematics, ICT, Physics), (2) band choices, (3) school principal’s nominations, and (4) OEA.…




                  
                  🎓 Admission talk Q6 — how competitive it is · ⬅ back to cover page
                  
                

Question
If two students have the same JUPAS score, who gets the offer?
Answer
CityUHK’s published JS1204 selection criteria say that with equal scores, the university refers to: (1) results in discipline-related subjects (e.g., Mathematics, ICT, Physics), (2) band choices, (3) school principal’s nominations, and (4) OEA. Additionally, the university’s general notes confirm that besides the main admission score, other scores and factors considered include subject results, band choices, and interview performance where applicable.
For JS1204 there is no scheduled interview, so in practice the tie-breakers are discipline subject results first, then band choice (earlier band = stronger preference signal), then SPN/OEA.
Examples

Two 23.0-point applicants for JS1204: Student A has Math 5* and put CS in Band A; Student B has Math 4 and put CS in Band B. Student A ranks ahead on discipline subject + band preference.

Question
How is the JUPAS admission score for BSc Computer Science calculated?
Answer
JS1204 BSc Computer Science (2026 JUPAS):


Subjects included: your best 5 subjects (Category A), excluding CSD and Liberal Studies.


Weightings: all at 1.


2026 flexible admissions threshold: score above 23 for consideration under the flexible arrangement.


2026 published admissions scores (from 2025-entry main-round offers): Median 23, Lower Quartile 22.


Important: although the university has discussed 1.5x weightings for English/Mathematics/ICT/M1/M2/Physics/Chemistry/Biology for CS, the officially published 2026 JUPAS formula for JS1204 is best-5 at weight 1. The 1.5x discussion is a proposed policy that is not yet reflected in the published JS1204 formula - see the dedicated note for status.
Examples

A student’s best 5 countable subjects: Eng 5 (5.5), Math 5 (5.5), ICT 4 (4), Physics 4 (4), Economics 4 (4) => 23.0. This equals the 2026 median - a realistic target for a competitive applicant.

JUPAS Band Choices Explained


                  
                  Short answer 
                  
                

In JUPAS you list up to 10 programme choices, each in one of three bands: Band A (up to 3 choices), Band B (up to 3), Band C (up to 4). You can hold at most one offer in each band. Band A is for your strongest preferences. For a student who wants…




                  
                  🎓 Admission talk Q6 — how competitive it is · ⬅ back to cover page
                  
                

Question
How do Band A, B and C choices work when applying to CS?
Answer
In JUPAS you list up to 10 programme choices, each in one of three bands: Band A (up to 3 choices), Band B (up to 3), Band C (up to 4). You can hold at most one offer in each band. Band A is for your strongest preferences. For a student who wants CityUHK CS, placing JS1204 in Band A signals it is a top choice - and band choice is explicitly used as a tie-breaker when admission scores are equal.
Strategy note: because CityUHK uses band choice in tie-breaking, and because a Band A offer must be accepted before you can be considered for Band B/C, put CS where you would genuinely want to go. A common strong setup: Band A = CityUHK CS + HKU Computing/CS + HKUST CS&E; Band B = CUHK CS + PolyU Computing + CityUHK Cybersecurity; Band C = safety computing/data programmes.
Examples

Student lists JS1204 in Band A (choice 1) and JS1218 in Band B. If offered CS in the Main Round, accepting it closes the Band A slot; the Band B offer (Cybersecurity) would only matter if the Band A offer was declined.

What is the JUPAS Flexible Admission Arrangement and what does the threshold score mean?

The Flexible Admissions Arrangement lets CityUHK consider applicants who fall slightly short of the main admission score but meet a lower threshold, typically when their weaker subject is exactly at the minimum required level. OEA and Principal’s Nominations for CityUHK CS


                  
                  Short answer 
                  
                

Yes, but only in specific ways. Under JUPAS you can submit OEA (Other Experiences and Achievements in Competitions/Activities) - e.g., a nationally ranked olympiad in math or informatics, robotics, or IT projects. CityUHK’s selection criteria for…




                  
                  🎓 Admission talk Q7 — JUPAS interview? · ⬅ back to cover page
                  
                

Question
Can competition achievements or a principal’s nomination help me get into CS?
Answer
Yes, but only in specific ways. Under JUPAS you can submit OEA (Other Experiences and Achievements in Competitions/Activities) - e.g., a nationally ranked olympiad in math or informatics, robotics, or IT projects. CityUHK’s selection criteria for JS1204 state that for students with the same admission score, reference is made to other information such as results in discipline-related subjects, band choices, Principal’s Nominations, and OEA. So OEA/SPN act primarily as tie-breakers and supplementary considerations, not as a substitute for the admission score.
Principal’s Nominations (SPN) are submitted by your school (deadline 10 May 2027 for 2027 cycle) and can carry special consideration feedback announced 9 July 2027. For CS, the strongest OEA evidence is informatics olympiads, math olympiads, and substantial self-directed software projects.
Examples

Two students both scoring 23 on JS1204: the one with a national ICPC-style team placement and an SPN has the edge in tie-breaking.

01_jupas-basics/subject-weightings-in-ju.title: Subject Weightings in JUPAS Admission Scores
01_jupas-basics/subject-weightings-in-ju.content:
Subject Weightings in JUPAS Admission Scores


                  
                  Short answer 
                  
                

CityUHK weights each subject differently per programme. A subject marked “1.5” contributes 1.5 x its level points to the total; “2” contributes 2x, etc. The admission score is the sum over the subjects in the programme’s formula.




                  
                  🎓 Admission talk Q5 — the NEW 1.5x weighting policy · ⬅ back to cover page
                  
                

Question
What does ‘weighting’ mean and how is it applied in CityUHK’s admission score?
Answer
CityUHK weights each subject differently per programme. A subject marked “1.5” contributes 1.5 x its level points to the total; “2” contributes 2x, etc. The admission score is the sum over the subjects in the programme’s formula.
For example, the BBA Global Business formula (JS1001) weights English at 1.5 and everything else at 1: a student with English 5 (5.5 points) and four 4s (4 each) gets 5.5*1.5 + 4+4+4+4 = 8.25 + 16 = 24.25 (using best 5 including English).
Most CityUHK computing programmes in 2026 use flat weight 1 for JS1204, JS1218 and JS1221 (best 5 subjects), while the data-science programmes weight Mathematics at 2 and English at 1.5 (3 core + 2 elective subjects formula).
Examples

JS1072 BSc Data Science 2026 formula: 3 core (English, Chinese, Math) + 2 electives, weights 2:Mathematics, 1.5:English, 1:others. A student with Eng 5, Chi 4, Math 5*, ICT 5, Physics 4 scores 5.51.5 + 4 + 72 + 5.5 + 4 = 8.25+4+14+5.5+4 = 35.75 - but note ‘best 5 / 3 core+2 elective’ selection rules can change which subjects count.

02_jupas-scores/jupas-admissions-scores-.content:
JUPAS Admissions Scores: What Median and Lower Quartile Mean


                  
                  Short answer 
                  
                

CityUHK reports two reference scores per programme, computed from the HKDSE results of applicants who received Main Round offers in the prior entry:


Question
What do ‘median’ and ‘lower quartile’ admission scores actually mean?
Answer
CityUHK reports two reference scores per programme, computed from the HKDSE results of applicants who received Main Round offers in the prior entry:


Median: the admission score of the applicant sitting in the middle of the admission list. Roughly half of those admitted had a score at or above this.


Lower Quartile: the admission score of the applicant at 3/4 of the way down the list (i.e., 25% of admits scored below this). It is the approximate floor of the admitted cohort.


These are reference points, not cut-offs. CityUHK explicitly says scores are not comparable across programmes or years and should not be used to predict your chance of admission - the decision also weighs subject results, band choices and (where applicable) interviews.
Examples

For JS1204 in 2026, a score of 23 (median) means you’d be around the middle of last year’s admitted class; a score of 22 (lower quartile) means you’d be near the bottom of it.

02_jupas-scores/typical-admission-compet.content:
Typical Admission Competitiveness: Most Admits Come From Band A


                  
                  Short answer 
                  
                

CityUHK CS is among the more competitive local computing programmes but sits below HKU/HKUST top-ranked computing in raw JUPAS scores. The 2026 median JS1204 score of 23 corresponds to a typical admitted profile of roughly 544AA-plus in the…




                  
                  🎓 Admission talk Q6 — how competitive it is · ⬅ back to cover page
                  
                

Question
How competitive is CityUHK CS and do I need Band A results?
Answer
CityUHK CS is among the more competitive local computing programmes but sits below HKU/HKUST top-ranked computing in raw JUPAS scores. The 2026 median JS1204 score of 23 corresponds to a typical admitted profile of roughly 544AA-plus in the countable subjects - i.e., most admits come from the Band A cohort (top performers). The 2026 lower quartile of 22 is the floor of the main-round admits.
Concretely, a 23-point profile usually looks like: English 5, Mathematics 5, and three 4s (444) or two 5s and three 4s. Students with 443AA (best 5 around 19-21) are typically at or below the lower quartile and would be borderline - where the flexible admission arrangement and tie-breakers matter.
Because selection is score-first with no blanket interview, a strong 5-5-4-4-4 profile in CS-relevant subjects is the reliable path into a Band A offer for JS1204.
Examples

A student with Eng 5, Math 5, ICT 4, Physics 4, Chem 4 (23.0) is right at the 2026 median and a realistic Band A candidate. A student with Eng 4, Math 4, ICT 4, Physics 3, Econ 3 (19.0) is below the lower quartile (22) and would need OEA/SPN or a lower programme as a safety.

02_jupas-scores/why-cityuhk-cs-scores-ar.content:
Why CityUHK CS Scores Are Not Comparable Across Years


                  
                  Short answer 
                  
                

Three reasons. (1) Conversion scale changed: from 2025 entry, Category A levels map to 5=8.5, 5*=7, 5=5.5, 4=4, 3=3, 2=2, 1=1. Before that, the scale was different, so a ‘20’ in 2024 is not the same as a ‘20’ in 2025. (2) Weightings change per p


Question
Why can’t I just compare my score to last year’s admitted score directly?
Answer
Three reasons. (1) Conversion scale changed: from 2025 entry, Category A levels map to 5**=8.5, 5*=7, 5=5.5, 4=4, 3=3, 2=2, 1=1. Before that, the scale was different, so a ‘20’ in 2024 is not the same as a ‘20’ in 2025. (2) Weightings change per programme per year - e.g., a programme may weight Math at 2 one year and 1 the next. (3) Applicant pools shift each year in size and strength.
CityUHK’s official note says: ‘As different weightings are used, admissions scores are not comparable across programmes or admission years. The admissions scores below are for reference only and should not be used to predict the likelihood of admission.’ So treat the published median/lower quartile for the current year’s formula as your guide, and confirm the formula in the year you apply.

Worked Example Computing JS1204 Admission Score


                  
                  Short answer 
                  
                

Formula (2026, published): best 5 countable subjects, each at weight 1, using the 2025+ conversion (5**=8.5, 5*=7, 5=5.5, 4=4, 3=3, 2=2, 1=1). CSD and Liberal Studies are excluded.




                  
                  🎓 Admission talk Q4 — how the JUPAS score is calculated · ⬅ back to cover page
                  
                

Question
Can you show me how to actually compute a JS1204 admission score from HKDSE results?
Answer
Formula (2026, published): best 5 countable subjects, each at weight 1, using the 2025+ conversion (5**=8.5, 5*=7, 5=5.5, 4=4, 3=3, 2=2, 1=1). CSD and Liberal Studies are excluded.
Example 1: HKDSE results: English 5, Chinese 4, Mathematics 5, ICT 4, Physics 4, Economics 3.
Convert: Eng 5.5, Chi 4, Math 5.5, ICT 4, Phy 4, Econ 3. Best 5 (drop the 3): 5.5 + 5.5 + 4 + 4 + 4 = 23.0. This equals the 2026 median - a solid applicant.
Example 2: English 5*, Mathematics 5*, ICT 5, Physics 4, Chemistry 3. Convert: 7 + 7 + 5.5 + 4 + 3 = 26.5. Strongly above the 2026 median of 23.
Example 3 (weaker): English 4, Mathematics 3, ICT 3, Physics 3, Economics 3. Best 5: 4 + 3 + 3 + 3 + 3 = 16.0. Below the flexible threshold of 23 - not competitive for JS1204.
Examples

To beat the 2026 lower quartile (22) you need roughly a profile like 5/5/4/4/4 or 5*/4/4/4/4 across your best five countable subjects.

Advanced Standing I (Year 2) Admission


                  
                  Short answer 
                  
                

Advanced Standing I (ASI) admits students to Year 2 of a four-year degree, so they take fewer credits to graduate (minimum 90-91 credit units instead of 120-121). It is the main ‘direct entry’ route for AD/HD holders into CS.

Question
What is Advanced Standing I and how do I start CityUHK CS in Year 2?
Answer
Advanced Standing I (ASI) admits students to Year 2 of a four-year degree, so they take fewer credits to graduate (minimum 90-91 credit units instead of 120-121). It is the main ‘direct entry’ route for AD/HD holders into CS. For the coming year ASI is available for BOTH BSc Computer Science (JS1204) and BSc Cybersecurity (JS1218).
To be eligible for ASI in CS you generally need: a final-year or graduated Associate Degree / Higher Diploma (or equivalent) in a computing-related discipline, meeting the General Entrance Requirements. Students admitted with ASI are not entitled to further credit transfer; instead they may be granted course exemptions based on prior study (no credit units are earned for exempted courses).
For BSc Cybersecurity specifically, senior-year/ASI applicants are normally expected to have completed the AD/HD with CGPA >= 3.0 or an equivalent overall mark or credit award. Indicative intake for BSc Cybersecurity (29 local places) covers both first-year and ASI entries combined.
The non-JUPAS code for ASI in CS is 1561A (BSc Computer Science) and 1720A (BSc Cybersecurity). Applications close 30 Apr 2026 for the 2026 cycle (per the CS department page).
Examples

An associate-degree graduate in Computing Technology with CGPA 3.4 applies via code 1561A with ASI and, if admitted, starts directly in CS Year 2, graduating in about 3 years.

Advanced Standing II (Senior Year) Admission


                  
                  Short answer 
                  
                

Advanced Standing II (ASII), also called senior-year admission, admits students to the final (Year 3) year of a four-year degree, taking a minimum of 60 credit units instead of 120-121. It is only available to local students.




                  
                  🎓 Admission talk Q8 — non-JUPAS routes · ⬅ back to cover page
                  
                

Question
What is Advanced Standing II and can I join CS in the final year?
Answer
Advanced Standing II (ASII), also called senior-year admission, admits students to the final (Year 3) year of a four-year degree, taking a minimum of 60 credit units instead of 120-121. It is only available to local students. For the coming year ASII is available for BOTH BSc Computer Science (JS1204) and BSc Cybersecurity (JS1218).
Eligibility: final-year students or graduates of an AD/HD programme recognized by CityUHK. No CGPA or overall-mark requirement is set for applying, but because competition is keen, accepted applicants are normally expected to have completed AD/HD with CGPA 3.0 or an equivalent overall mark, or a credit award. Individual programmes may set higher requirements.
For CS and Cybersecurity, the major entrance requirement is holding an AD/HD in a computing-related discipline (or equivalent). Offers to final-year applicants are conditional on attaining the AD/HD award with the specified CGPA/overall mark/award classification.
ASII gives the fastest route into CS - essentially finishing the final year (or the last segment) of the degree after two years of sub-degree study.
Examples

A final-year Higher Diploma in IT student with CGPA 3.1 applies for ASII (code 1720A for Cybersecurity) and, on graduating HD with credit, completes the senior year to earn the BSc.

Answer

Answer


Create an account at cityu.edu.hk/admo/apply-now.


Select the programme (e.g., 1561A BSc CS, 1720A BSc Cybersecurity) and choose your entry type (Year 1 / ASI / ASII where offered).

Question
What is non-JUPAS Year 1 admission and who can use it?
Answer
Non-JUPAS Year 1 admission is CityUHK’s route for local applicants who do NOT use HKDSE/JUPAS. It is open to: current students or graduates of a recognized Associate Degree (AD) or Higher Diploma (HD); students or graduates of high school following a non-HKDSE curriculum (IB, GCE A Level/IAL); and transfer students from local or overseas bachelor’s programmes.
You must meet the General Entrance Requirements plus any programme-specific requirements. Applications are made at cityu.edu.hk/admo/apply-now with a fee of HK$200 per programme. For CS, the relevant codes are 1561A (BSc Computer Science) and 1720A (BSc Cybersecurity).
Admission is competitive - meeting minimum qualifications does not guarantee acceptance. Final-year AD/HD applicants receive conditional offers subject to attaining the award with a specified CGPA/overall mark.

Yes, via non-JUPAS. Transfer students from local or overseas bachelor’s degree programmes may apply; ‘Bachelor’s degree study of one year or more / postgraduate study’ is listed as an eligible qualification for first-year and ASI entry. BSc Cybersecurity (JS1218) shares the same first-year base as CS (programming, calculus, linear algebra, computer organisation) and the same core CS courses, but adds a cybersecurity focus. The curriculum is described as a set of highly focused…


Question
What does the BSc Cybersecurity curriculum consist of?
Answer
BSc Cybersecurity (JS1218) shares the same first-year base as CS (programming, calculus, linear algebra, computer organisation) and the same core CS courses, but adds a cybersecurity focus. The curriculum is described as a set of highly focused core courses (operating systems, problem solving and analysis, programming and modelling, data structures, software security and design, communication skills and professional knowledge) plus a wide range of electives covering information security and management, machine learning, mobile, software engineering and quality management, distributed systems and cloud computing.
The five features/specialisations are: System Security, Software Security, Cryptography, Privacy-Enhancing Technologies, and Cyber Risk Management. Representative CS-department security courses include CS2117 Foundation of Cybersecurity, CS2612 Seminars on Contemporary Cybersecurity, CS3273 Data Protection and System Security, CS3104 Applied Cryptographic Systems, CS4101 Software Security, CS4191 Mobile and IoT Security, CS4288 Cryptographic Algorithms and Protocols, CS4286 Internet Security and e-Commerce Protocols, CS4293 Topics in Cybersecurity, and CS4394 Information Security and Management.

CS students undertake a major design and development project (CS4514 Project / CS4552 Guided Study) in areas such as e-commerce, virtual reality, multimedia, computer vision, cloud computing, information security and data science. Answer
Both are 4-year degrees in the same College of Computing and share the first-year base and much of the CS core. The difference is focus and outcomes:


BSc CS (JS1204) is the broad discipline: you can specialise in AI, Cybersecurity, Data Science, Multimedia, or Software Engineering - it is the ‘parent’ programme with the widest choice, including the standalone Cybersecurity stream.


BSc Cybersecurity (JS1218) is a dedicated, narrower degree where security is the through-line (system security, software security, cryptography, privacy-enhancing technologies, cyber risk management). You graduate with a degree titled in Cybersecurity, which signals a security specialisation to employers.


In short: choose CS for maximum flexibility (you can still go deep into security via its Cybersecurity stream); choose Cybersecurity if you are certain you want a security-focused identity and curriculum. The admission score for JS1218 (2026: 20.5) has been slightly below JS1204 (23), reflecting it being newer and more specialised.
Examples

A student who loves building systems broadly -> JS1204 CS (pick the AI or SE stream). A student who specifically wants to be a security engineer/cryptographer/risk analyst -> JS1218 Cybersecurity. Both can take each other’s electives.

CityUHK’s CS college requirement includes MA1508 Calculus (4 CU) and MA1503 Linear Algebra with Applications (4 CU). These are not decoration: modern CS - especially AI, machine learning, computer graphics, and optimisation - is built on linear…


Question
Why does CS require Calculus and Linear Algebra in Year 1?
Answer
CityUHK’s CS college requirement includes MA1508 Calculus (4 CU) and MA1503 Linear Algebra with Applications (4 CU). These are not decoration: modern CS - especially AI, machine learning, computer graphics, and optimisation - is built on linear algebra (vectors, matrices, transformations) and calculus (gradients, optimization). Courses like CS4487 Machine Learning and CS4489 Optimization Foundations for AI Training assume these foundations.
For applicants: this is why a strong Mathematics DSE result matters for CS. A Level 3 in Mathematics is the minimum, but students who struggle with calculus/linear algebra will find the AI and Data Science streams harder. If you want CS but find pure math weak, the Software Engineering and Multimedia streams are somewhat less math-heavy than AI.

Question
What does the BSc Computer Science curriculum look like?
Answer
BSc CS is a 4-year degree (~120 credit units) built in four layers: (1) Gateway Education (31 CU) - Chinese Civilisation, University English + discipline-specific English, Whole-Person Development, and distributional areas; (2) College-specified courses (Computing) - e.g., CS1302A Introduction to Computer Programming; (3) College Requirement - MA1508 Calculus (4 CU) and MA1503 Linear Algebra with Applications (4 CU); and (4) Major Requirements - CS core courses plus 15 CU of electives.
First year (33 CU) includes: GE1501 Chinese Civilisation, English (3 CU), CS1302A Introduction to Computer Programming, GE1601 Whole-Person Development, 3 CU distributional, Calculus, Linear Algebra, and core courses CS2115 Computer Organisation, CS2310 Computer Programming, CS2402 Introduction to Computational Probability Modeling.
Students then specialise in one of five streams by taking 3 courses of the chosen stream (or any 5 electives if they prefer a mix). The curriculum is HKIE-accredited - the first CS programme in Hong Kong to receive that accreditation.

04_curriculum/itpp-it-professional-inter.content:
ITPP IT Professional Internship Overview


                  
                  Short answer 
                  
                

The IT Professional Internship (ITPP) is a mandatory, credit-bearing, 9-month placement taken in the third year (after completing the first two years of full-time study). It is an integral component of the CS curriculum - all students acquire…




                  
                  🎓 Admission talk Q2 — the mandatory 9-month internship · ⬅ back to cover page
                  
                

Question
What is the mandatory IT Professional Internship (ITPP) in CS?
Answer
The IT Professional Internship (ITPP) is a mandatory, credit-bearing, 9-month placement taken in the third year (after completing the first two years of full-time study). It is an integral component of the CS curriculum - all students acquire working experience before graduation. This is a major, explicit differentiator versus many programmes elsewhere that treat internships as optional.
During ITPP, students work in real IT-related projects/developments at companies or government organisations, learning to work as a team member in business or government settings. Students work 4 days a week with Fridays off to attend classes at CityUHK, so the internship runs alongside a study load rather than fully pausing the degree.
Performance is jointly assessed by an academic supervisor (CityUHK) and a working supervisor (the employer). Employers interview students before the placement is confirmed and assign a working supervisor; companies are invited each November/December and post jobs from December/January.

04_curriculum/minor-in-artificial-intell.content:
Minor in Artificial Intelligence


                  
                  Short answer 
                  
                

Yes - a 15-CU minor (core CS4486 Artificial Intelligence + 12 CU from Machine Learning, Computer Vision, NLP, Generative AI, AI Game Programming or Optimization for AI Training). Declaration needs CGPA 3.0+, home-department approval and a passed programming course; the award needs GPA 2.0 in the 15 minor credits. Ideal for non-CS majors (Business, Science, Liberal Studies) to add credible AI depth.


Question
Can non-CS students take a Minor in Artificial Intelligence?
Answer
Yes. CityUHK offers a Minor in Artificial Intelligence (15 credit units) that students from other programmes can declare to add structured AI coursework to their degree:

Core (3 CU): CS4486 Artificial Intelligence.
Electives (12 CU, choose 4): CS4186 Computer Vision and Image Processing, CS4386 AI Game Programming, CS4487 Machine Learning, CS4489 Optimization Foundations for AI Training, CS4490 Generative AI Essentials and Applications, CS4493 Natural Language Processing.
To declare: CGPA 3.0 or above, advance approval from your home department, and a passed programming course (CS2311 / CS2313 Computer Programming or CS2360 Java Programming).
To receive the award: 15 CU of minor courses with an average GPA of 2.0 in those courses.

There is also a broader Minor in Computing for non-CS majors who want core computing skills (programming, networking, web systems) rather than AI specialisation.
For a CS major the AI minor is partly redundant (the AI stream already covers these courses), but for a student in, say, Business or Data Science, the AI minor is the cheapest way to add credible AI depth. It is a useful ‘flexibility’ talking point: CityUHK computing is modular, so you can layer AI onto other degrees. Because it is declared after entry, it does not change JUPAS requirements.

04_curriculum/why-the-mandatory-internsh.content:
Why the Mandatory Internship Matters


                  
                  Short answer 
                  
                

It removes the single biggest objection parents and students have about a CS degree - ‘will this get me a job?’. Because ITPP is mandatory, every CS graduate leaves with a full 9-month, industry-supervised work experience and a reference from a…




                  
                  🎓 Admission talk Q2 — the mandatory 9-month internship · ⬅ back to cover page
                  
                

Question
Why does the mandatory internship matter so much for a CS applicant?
Answer
It removes the single biggest objection parents and students have about a CS degree - ‘will this get me a job?’. Because ITPP is mandatory, every CS graduate leaves with a full 9-month, industry-supervised work experience and a reference from a real employer, at a point in their degree when they are still a student. In a competitive first-job market, this is a concrete, verifiable edge over graduates from programmes without a built-in placement.
It also de-risks the choice of stream: students discover what industry work actually feels like (banking, government, telecom, software houses) before they finalise specialisation. The internship is directly tied to the department’s 97.5% full-time employment outcome, which is the headline stat the admissions team wants you to remember.
Examples

A CS student interning at the HK Monetary Authority or Huawei during Year 3 leaves with that employer on their CV and a joint academic+industrial grade - a strong first-job signal that a typical 4-year CS degree without placement cannot match.

05_programmes/bsc-data-science-vs-cs-dat.content:
BSc Data Science vs CS Data Science Stream


                  
                  Short answer 
                  
                

Decide by what the ‘core’ of your degree should be:


Question
Should I choose BSc Data Science or the CS Data Science stream?
Answer
Decide by what the ‘core’ of your degree should be:


BSc Data Science (JS1072): the degree is data science. Strongest if you want a data-science identity, are strong in maths/statistics, and less concerned with building large software systems. Formula: 3 core + 2 electives, Math x2.


CS Data Science stream (within JS1204): the degree is Computer Science with a data specialisation. You get the full CS core (software engineering, operating systems, networks, algorithms) plus the mandatory internship, and you specialise in data. Formula: best 5, weight 1.


Rule of thumb: want the software-engineering credibility + guaranteed industry placement? JS1204 CS (Data Science stream). Want a focused, data-first degree with heavier maths weighting? JS1072 BSc Data Science. Both are in the same College of Computing and share first-year courses, so switching later is relatively low-cost.
Examples

A student with Math 5*, Statistics/ICT 5 and interest in analytics but little desire to do systems programming -> JS1072. A student who wants to build products and also use data -> JS1204 CS with the Data Science stream and the ITPP internship.

05_programmes/double-degree-requirements.title: Double Degree Requirements and Structure
05_programmes/double-degree-requirements.content:
Double Degree Requirements and Structure


                  
                  Short answer 
                  
                

CityUHK runs two CS double degrees. JS1221 (CS + Computational Finance & FinTech): 5 years, 151 CU minimum, JUPAS Math 4. JS1063 (LLB + BSc CS AI stream, new 2027/28): 5 years, 158 CU, JUPAS English 5. Both charge self-financing fees for credits above 144 in years 1-4 and all year-5 credits.




                  
                  🎓 Admission talk Q9 — the double degrees · ⬅ back to cover page
                  
                

Question
How do the CS double degrees work in terms of requirements?
Answer
JS1221 (BSc CS + BSc Computational Finance & FinTech). A 5-year double degree requiring a minimum of 151 credit units for the double-degree award. The structure splits requirements between the two degrees:

University & Distributional Requirements: 22 CU (University English, discipline-specific English, Chinese Civilisation, Whole-Person Development, 12 CU distributional).
College-specified courses: 18 CU total (9 CU computing-specified + 9 CU business-specified).
College/School Requirement: 12 CU.
Major Required Courses: 99 CU, of which 33 CU are CS core, 30 CU are Computational Finance/FinTech core, 33 CU serve as core or electives for both majors, and 3 CU are one CS elective.

JUPAS minimums: Eng 3, Chi 3, Math 4, CSD attained, plus a Level-3 relevant elective and a second Level-3 elective.
JS1063 (LLB + BSc Computer Science, AI stream). New for 2027/28 (8 local JUPAS places): 5 years, 158 credit units (58 CU CS/AI courses + 57 CU law courses + gateway/English). JUPAS minimums: English 5, Math 3, Chinese 3, CSD attained, a Level-3 science/ICT elective (Physics/ICT/M1/M2/Biology/Chemistry) and a second Level-3 elective. The LLB is a qualifying law degree (PCLL route). See JS1063 LLB and BScCS Double Degree Overview for the full detail.
Common cost rule. For both double degrees, credits above 144 completed in the first four years and any credits taken in year 5 and beyond are charged on a self-financing basis — so the cost/time premium of a double degree is real and should be planned for.

05_programmes/js1063-llb-and-bsccs-doubl.title: JS1063 LLB and BSc Computer Science (AI) Double Degree Overview
05_programmes/js1063-llb-and-bsccs-doubl.content:
JS1063 LLB and BSc Computer Science (AI) Double Degree Overview


                  
                  Short answer 
                  
                

JS1063 is a brand-new 5-year double degree (first intake 2027/28, 8 local JUPAS places) run jointly by the School of Law and the Department of Computer Science: a qualifying LLB plus a BSc Computer Science (Stream: Artificial Intelligence) in 5 years instead of the ~8 for two separate degrees. JUPAS minimums are English 5, Math 3, Chinese 3, CSD attained, plus a Level-3 science/ICT elective (Physics / ICT / M1 / M2 / Biology / Chemistry) and a second Level-3 elective. First-year fee HK$49,500; credits above 144 in year 1-4 and all year-5 credits are self-financing.




                  
                  🎓 Admission talk Q9 — the double degrees · ⬅ back to cover page
                  
                

Question
What is the LLB + BSc Computer Science (AI) double degree (JS1063), and who is it for?
Answer
What it is. A 5-year interdisciplinary double degree between the School of Law and the Department of Computer Science, designed for the law-and-technology intersection: AI and legal tech, data privacy, intellectual property in computing, and legal analysis backed by technical ability. Graduates earn two degrees: a qualifying LLB (the one needed to start the path to becoming a lawyer) and a BSc in Computer Science with the Artificial Intelligence stream.
Requirements (JUPAS, JS1063):

































SubjectMinimum levelEnglish LanguageLevel 5 (higher than JS1204/JS1218, which need 3)Chinese LanguageLevel 3Mathematics (compulsory)Level 3Citizenship and Social DevelopmentAttainedElective 1: Physics / ICT / M1 / M2 / Biology / ChemistryLevel 3Elective 2: any subjectLevel 3
M1 and M2 count as one subject; Category C other languages can also satisfy the elective. Non-JUPAS applicants need the general English-profiency standard (e.g. IELTS band 7 overall or equivalent, within two years) and there is no advanced-standing entry.
Structure and cost. 158 credit units total (58 CU CS/AI + 57 CU law, plus gateway/English courses). Core law courses include Legal Methods, HK Legal System, Contract, Tort, Constitutional, Administrative, Criminal, Land Law, Jurisprudence, PRC Public and Private Law, Equity & Trusts, Company Law; core CS includes Computer Organization, Programming, Operating Systems, Networks, Data Structures, Software Design, Algorithms, Artificial Intelligence, Machine Learning, Project, Discrete Mathematics. Credits above 144 in the first four years and all 5th-year credits are charged self-financing, so plan for the cost premium. First-year tuition 2027/28: HK$49,500.
Entry and size. New for 2027/28 with an indicative local intake of 8 places — expect a high, uncapped competition; it is marked “New” in JUPAS with no historical scores yet. Interview and/or test may be required. Admissions contact: lw.dd.cs@cityu.edu.hk.
Careers. Two doors: (1) the qualifying LLB plus two PCLL pre-requisite electives satisfies the requirements to apply for the PCLL (path to barrister/solicitor); (2) the BSc CS (AI) is HKIE-accredited with Seoul Accord reciprocity (AU, CA, IL, NZ, ZA, UK, US) — software/AI roles. The combination is aimed at legal-tech, compliance, IP, and data-governance careers.
Special features. Small tutorial groups; guest lectures from top overseas law schools; G-LEAP (month-long course at University College, Oxford / University of Melbourne); international mooting support; exchanges across ~17 countries; CityUHK Law Review; legal placements at law firms, banks, international companies and NGOs.
Current-student transfer in. CityU students can apply to transfer into the programme with CGPA 3.30 plus good English proficiency (e.g. HKDSE English Level 5, IELTS 7, or equivalent).
How it differs from JS1221. JS1221 pairs CS with Computational Finance & FinTech (business careers, lower JUPAS English requirement: 3). JS1063 pairs CS (AI stream) with Law and has a much higher English requirement (5) — choose JS1063 only if law is genuinely part of the career plan, because the LLB commitment (and PCLL route) is substantial.
Examples

A student with English 5, Math 5, Chinese 4, M1 4, ICT 4, Physics 4 meets all JS1063 minimums (English 5 is the binding constraint for most applicants).
The same profile also meets JS1204/JS1221 minimums, so JS1063 is about the career direction (law + tech), not just admission feasibility.
Cost planning: years 1-4 on UGC rates, then self-financing from the 145th credit onward (year 5) — meaningfully more expensive than a 4-year single degree.

JS1070 ACT Programme Overview

JS1070 ‘AI, Computing and Transformation (ACT)’ (called DELTA in 2025) is a College of Computing programme with a free choice of major plus signature features: one-to-one advisor, elite work placement, executive mentor scheme, premium overseas…


Question
What is the ACT programme (JS1070) and how is it different from CS?
Answer
JS1070 ‘AI, Computing and Transformation (ACT)’ (called DELTA in 2025) is a College of Computing programme with a free choice of major plus signature features: one-to-one advisor, elite work placement, executive mentor scheme, premium overseas exchange, and internship exchange. Its 2026 formula is 3 core + 2 elective subjects with weights 2:English/Mathematics, 1:others; 2026 score median 31 / lower quartile 30; flexible threshold above 31.
Compared with JS1204 CS: ACT is more elite/selective (higher score, mentorship + placement model) and lets you choose the major after entry, whereas JS1204 is a direct-entry CS degree with stream specialisation. Think of ACT as the ‘honours/transformative’ computing track and JS1204 as the standard, broadly available CS degree with the mandatory internship.

Question
What is the Data Science Majors programme (JS1071)?
Answer
JS1071 ‘Data Science’ is a College of Computing programme offering two majors: BSc Data Science and BSc Data and Systems Engineering, with free choice of major after entry. Its 2026 formula is 3 core + 2 elective subjects with weights 2:Mathematics, 1.5:English, 1:others; 2026 score median 27.5 / lower quartile 27.5; flexible threshold above 27.5.
The 3 core + 2 elective formula (instead of best 5) and the heavier Mathematics weighting mean this programme rewards strong maths more than JS1204 CS. It is the natural home for students whose strength is quantitative data work rather than software engineering.

05_programmes/js1204-bsc-computer-scienc.content:
JS1204 BSc Computer Science Overview


                  
                  Short answer 
                  
                

BSc Computer Science (JS1204) is the flagship 4-year programme of the Department of Computer Science, offering a well-balanced curriculum in both the theoretical and practical aspects of computing, with five streams: Artificial Intelligence, Cybersecurity, Data Science, Multimedia Computing, and Software Engineering and Project Management.




                  
                  🎓 Admission talk Q1 — what makes the majors attractive · ⬅ back to cover page
                  
                

Question
What is BSc Computer Science (JS1204) at CityUHK?
Answer
BSc Computer Science (JS1204) is the flagship 4-year programme of the Department of Computer Science, offering a well-balanced curriculum in both the theoretical and practical aspects of computing, with five streams: Artificial Intelligence, Cybersecurity, Data Science, Multimedia Computing, and Software Engineering and Project Management.
Key features: a focused core plus wide electives; the mandatory 9-month IT Professional Internship (all students work before graduating); HKIE accreditation (first CS programme in HK); 97.5% full-time employment (2024 survey); and a joint Bachelor’s Degree Programme with Columbia University (direct Year-1 admission from 2026/27).
Indicative local intake (2026/27): 85 places for JS1204 (first year + ASI combined). JUPAS minimums: Eng 3, Chi 3, Math 3, CSD attained, plus Level 3 in one of Bio/Chem/ICT/M1/M2/Physics and a second Level-3 elective. 2026 JUPAS score: median 23 / lower quartile 22 (best 5, weight 1).
Major leader (2026/27 page): Prof. Howard LEUNG (BEng McGill, MSc/PhD Carnegie Mellon). Enquiries: csadm@cityu.edu.hk, +852 3442 8580.

From the Graduate Employment Survey 2024 (BSc Computer Science), the headline outcome is 97.5% full-time employment (ratio of full-time employed graduates to total full-time/part-time employed and unemployed).
Employment sectors: Business Services 34.7%, Financial Institutions 13.3%, Government 13.3%, Engineering/Architectural/Technical Services 8%, Community/Social/Personal Services 6.7%, Trading 6.7%, Education 5.3%, Others 5.3%, Real Estate 2.7%, Construction 1.3%, Electricity/Gas/Steam 1.3%, Transport/Storage/Communications 1.3%.
Job nature: System Analysis and Computer Programmers 68.4%, Engineers 10.5%, Sales/Service 3.9%, Teaching and Research 3.9%, Business Professionals 7.9%, and small shares in other categories. This distribution confirms the degree is producing professional software/systems roles rather than a thin spread.

What is BSc Cybersecurity (JS1218) at CityUHK?
Answer
BSc Cybersecurity (JS1218) is a 4-year degree in the Department of Computer Science, newly launched (first JUPAS entry 2025) for the growing demand for skilled cybersecurity experts. It equips students to safeguard digital assets, respond to cyber threats and mitigate cybercrime risk.

Non-JUPAS code: 1720A (Year 1, ASI and ASII all available).

JS1221 Double Degree Overview


                  
                  Short answer 
                  
                

JS1221 is a 5-year double degree jointly offered by the Department of Computer Science and the College of Business, training professionals who blend computer science with computational finance and financial technology (AI, big data analytics, derivatives pricing, financial econometrics, portfolio management, software engineering, blockchain).




                  
                  🎓 Admission talk Q9 — the double degrees · ⬅ back to cover page
                  
                

Question
What is the BSc CS + BSc Computational Finance and FinTech double degree (JS1221)?
Answer
JS1221 is a 5-year double degree jointly offered by the Department of Computer Science and the College of Business, training professionals who blend computer science with computational finance and financial technology (AI, big data analytics, derivatives pricing, financial econometrics, portfolio management, software engineering, blockchain).
Indicative local intake (2026/27): 10 places (first-year entry). JUPAS minimums: Eng 3, Chi 3, Math 4, CSD attained, plus Level 3 in a relevant elective + a second Level-3 elective. 2026 JUPAS score: median 23 / lower quartile 22 (best 5, weight 1); flexible threshold above 23.
Graduates can pursue quantitative/finance/business analyst, cybersecurity analyst, AI/ML specialist, data scientist, risk & compliance specialist, or blockchain developer roles. Credits beyond the 4-year/144-CU norm and 5th-year credits are charged on a self-financing basis.

08_scholarships/ai-computing-and-transfo.title: AI Computing and Transformation (ACT) Flagship Scholarship
08_scholarships/ai-computing-and-transfo.content:
AI Computing and Transformation (ACT) Flagship Scholarship


                  
                  Short answer 
                  
                

JS1070 ACT (College of Computing) is one of the ten Flagship Programmes. Local JUPAS/non-JUPAS entrants with a minimum HKDSE scholarship score of 27.5 (half: 25) get 100% (or 50%) tuition and hall fees (double room) for the whole programme, plus exchange sponsorships up to HK$500,000 one-off.


Question
Does the new AI, Computing and Transformation (ACT) programme come with a scholarship?
Answer
Yes. ACT (JS1070) - the College of Computing’s programme in AI, computing and transformation - is listed among the ten Flagship Programmes, so its local entrants are eligible for Flagship Scholarships rather than the standard Institutional/Dean’s tiers:

Full Scholarship (minimum HKDSE scholarship score 27.5): 100% tuition and hall fees (double room occupancy), tenable for the programme’s full duration (4-6 years depending on the registered programme).
Half Scholarship (minimum 25): 50% tuition and hall fees (double room).
Exchange Sponsorships: up to HK$500,000 one-off for Flagship recipients.
Guaranteed hall berth for Flagship recipients.

ACT shares the flagship programme characteristics: globally oriented curriculum, overseas exchanges at top-ranked universities (on fulfilling conditions), and internationally oriented career preparation. Because a student admitted to ACT cannot simultaneously hold Institutional or Dean’s Scholarships, the Flagship award is the one that applies.
Note the score threshold uses the scholarship scoring scale (5** = 8.5, 5* = 7, 5 = 5.5, 4 = 4…), not the JUPAS level-point table - see Scholarship HKDSE Scoring Scale.
Examples

A student whose best-5 scholarship-scale score is 5** + 5 + 5 + 4 + 4 = 27.5, admitted to JS1070 ACT, receives the full Flagship Scholarship: zero tuition and zero hall fees (double room) for the entire programme.
The same student admitted to JS1204 instead would be limited to the Institutional/Dean’s tiers (max HK$94,000/yr tuition award) - so for strong candidates, ACT’s Flagship package is financially more generous.

08_scholarships/can-you-hold-multiple-ci.filePath: 08_Scholarships/Can You Hold Multiple CityUHK Scholarships (No Concurrent Awards).md
08_scholarships/can-you-hold-multiple-ci.title: Can You Hold Multiple CityUHK Scholarships (No Concurrent Awards)
08_scholarships/can-you-hold-multiple-ci.content:
Can You Hold Multiple CityUHK Scholarships (No Concurrent Awards)


                  
                  Short answer 
                  
                

No. JUPAS entrants cannot hold Flagship, Institutional and Dean’s Scholarships concurrently; non-JUPAS entrants cannot hold Flagship and Institutional concurrently. If you qualify for more than one, only the highest amount is awarded.


Question
I qualified for more than one scholarship - can I stack them?
Answer
No. The official rules are explicit:

JUPAS entrants are not allowed to hold Flagship, Institutional and Dean’s Scholarships concurrently.
Non-JUPAS entrants are not allowed to hold Flagship and Institutional Scholarships concurrently.
If an entrant is selected for more than one scholarship, only the scholarship with the highest amount is awarded.

So a strong JS1204 candidate who clears both the Institutional (HK69,000/yr) and Dean's Tier 1 (HK94,000/yr) thresholds simply receives the Dean’s Tier 1 award - they are not added together. In practice this means the Dean’s Tier 1 is the realistic ceiling for non-flagship local JUPAS programmes: HK94,000/yr beats both Institutional tiers (HK69,000/59,000/35,000). The separate one-off exchange scholarship (HK25,000 for Institutional recipients; up to HK500,000 for Flagship recipients) is a distinct exchange funding, not a second annual award.
These university-wide awards are also separate from donor scholarships (e.g. HSBC, Li Po Chun, Mapletree), which are additional and can be held alongside them.
Examples

A student with 4 subjects at 5** admitted to JS1204 qualifies for Institutional HK69,000/yr AND Dean's Tier 1 HK94,000/yr (score 27.5+) - they receive the HK$94,000/yr award only.
The same student can still be considered for, say, the HSBC Hong Kong Scholarship or donor awards during their studies - those are not part of the ‘no concurrent awards’ rule.

08_scholarships/cityuhk-scholarship-over.title: CityUHK Scholarship Overview
08_scholarships/cityuhk-scholarship-over.content:
CityUHK Scholarship Overview


                  
                  Short answer 
                  
                

CityUHK offers three university-wide entrance scholarships for local entrants (Flagship, Institutional, Dean’s) plus separate schemes for international, Chinese Mainland and student-athlete students. All are merit-based, need no separate application, and the biggest can cover 100% tuition (plus hall fees) for up to six years.




                  
                  🎓 Admission talk Q10 — scholarships and cost · ⬅ back to cover page
                  
                

Question
What scholarships are available for a student applying to a CityUHK CS programme?
Answer
CityUHK’s main award framework is the CityUHK Scholarships for Hong Kong Talents - set up for Hong Kong students with excellent HKDSE or GCE A-Level / IB results applying to government-funded bachelor’s programmes, with awards covering up to six years depending on the normal duration of the registered programme. It has three tiers:

Flagship Scholarships - for local JUPAS and non-JUPAS entrants admitted to one of ten flagship programmes (for CS students, the one that matters is JS1070 AI, Computing and Transformation (ACT) in the College of Computing).
Institutional Scholarships - for local JUPAS and non-JUPAS entrants in any other programme - this is the route for JS1204 BSc Computer Science and JS1218 BSc Cybersecurity.
Dean’s Scholarships - for local JUPAS entrants only, including JS1221 (BSc CS + BSc Computational Finance and Financial Technology) double degree.

Local JUPAS quick reference (2027 entry). The “scholarship score” is NOT the JUPAS level-point score: it is 3 core subjects (excluding Citizenship and Social Development) + 2 best electives on the scale 5** = 8.5, 5* = 7, 5 = 5.5, 4 = 4, 3 = 3, 2 = 2, 1 = 1 (see Scholarship HKDSE Scoring Scale).













































Award (CS-relevant)Minimum requirementValueFlagship - ACT JS1070 (full)score 27.5100% tuition + hall fees (double room), 4-6 yrs + exchange up to HK$500,000 one-off + guaranteed hall berthFlagship - ACT JS1070 (half)score 2550% tuition + hall feesDean’s Tier 1 (JS1204 / JS1218 / JS1221)score 27.5HK$94,000 per yearDean’s Tier 2 (JS1204 / JS1218 / JS1221)score 25HK$35,000 per yearInstitutional top tier (JS1204 / JS1218)4 subjects at 5 + Level 4 in Chinese or English****HK69,000 per year** + HK25,000 one-off exchangeInstitutional middle tier3 subjects at 5 + Level 4 in Chinese or English****HK59,000 per year** + HK25,000 one-off exchangeInstitutional entry tier2 subjects at 5 + Level 4 in Chinese or English** + score >= 25**HK35,000 per year** + HK25,000 one-off exchange
* All 5** from one sitting; M1/M2 count (both = one subject). ** If English is used for a 5**, Chinese must be Level 4+ (and vice versa).
Key rules: no separate application (awards are emailed with the JUPAS Main Round offer, 4 Aug 2027); the tiers are never stacked - if several apply, only the highest is paid (so a 27.5 JS1204 candidate gets Dean’s Tier 1, HK$94,000/yr, not Institutional); renewed each year on CGPA (Flagship: on continuing in the flagship programme); aimed at newly admitted students.
On top of these: a Diversity Grant and Entrance Scholarship Scheme (Top / Full Tuition / Half Tuition) for international students, scholarships for Chinese Mainland students (via Gaokao), Outstanding Athletes Entrance Scholarships, and 120+ donor scholarships for current students.
Examples

A local student admitted to JS1204 with 3 subjects at 5** can receive the Institutional Scholarship of HK59,000 per year for 4 years (plus a one-off HK25,000 exchange scholarship) - roughly HK236,000+ against about HK188,000 of total tuition.
A local student admitted to JS1070 ACT with a scholarship score of 27.5 gets the ACT Flagship full scholarship: 100% tuition and hall fees (double room) for the whole programme.
A non-local (international) student admitted to JS1204 with top results can receive the Top Scholarship: HK$210,000 per year covering tuition, university-managed accommodation and partial living expenses.

08_scholarships/cityuhk-scholarships-for.title: CityUHK Scholarships for Chinese Mainland Students
08_scholarships/cityuhk-scholarships-for.content:
CityUHK Scholarships for Chinese Mainland Students


                  
                  Short answer 
                  
                

Chinese Mainland students admitted via the Gaokao route can receive entrance scholarships - including a full-tuition CityU Mainland Student Scholarship - assessed by merit with no separate application.


Question
Are there scholarships for Chinese Mainland students applying to CityUHK CS?
Answer
Yes. CityUHK runs a separate Entrance Scholarship track for Chinese Mainland students (Gaokao admission), distinct from the international student scheme. Published examples include the CityU Mainland Student Scholarship Scheme - Full Tuition Scholarship (学费全免奖学金), which covers the full tuition fee. As with the other university-wide entrance awards, selection is merit-based at admission and does not require a separate application - the appropriate award level is decided when the offer is made, and donors’ awards can be added on top.
Details (tiers, CGPA renewal conditions, number of awards) are published on the CityUHK admission site’s Chinese Mainland student section - check the current cycle’s page, since the Mainland scheme is listed separately from the international scheme and its terms are updated per cycle.
Examples

A Gaokao applicant admitted to JS1204 with a Full Tuition Mainland Scholarship pays no tuition for the degree, subject to the scheme’s annual renewal conditions.

08_scholarships/cityuhk-scholarships-for.title: CityUHK Scholarships for Hong Kong Talents
08_scholarships/cityuhk-scholarships-for.content:
CityUHK Scholarships for Hong Kong Talents


                  
                  Short answer 
                  
                

The umbrella scheme for local students (JUPAS and non-JUPAS) with excellent HKDSE or GCE A-Level / IB results. Three tiers - Flagship, Institutional, Dean’s - with awards covering up to six years depending on the registered programme’s normal duration.


Question
What is the ‘CityUHK Scholarships for Hong Kong Talents’ scheme and who is it for?
Answer
The scheme exists to attract bright local talent to government-funded bachelor’s degree programmes. It covers Hong Kong students with excellent HKDSE or GCE A-Level / IB results and is structured as:

























TierWho can get itTypical valueFlagship ScholarshipsLocal JUPAS and non-JUPAS entrants in one of the ten flagship programmes (CS: JS1070 ACT)100% or 50% tuition + hall fees (double room), up to 6 years, plus exchange sponsorships up to HK$500,000 one-offInstitutional ScholarshipsLocal JUPAS and non-JUPAS entrants in other programmes (incl. JS1204, JS1218)HK35,000-69,000 per year, 4-6 years, plus one-off HK25,000 exchange scholarshipDean’s ScholarshipsLocal JUPAS entrants only (incl. JS1204, JS1218, JS1221)HK94,000 (Tier 1) or HK35,000 (Tier 2) per year, 4-6 years
The scheme is primarily for newly admitted students; under special circumstances the University may consider re-admission candidates. Scholarship recipients also get dedicated benefits such as academic mentorship, overseas exchange opportunities, Golden Key Club membership and (for Flagship recipients) a guaranteed hall berth.
Examples

A student taking the IB route into JS1204 (code 1561A) is eligible for the Institutional Scholarship tier (GCE A-Level / IB criteria), not the Dean’s Scholarships, which are JUPAS-only.
The same local student cannot hold a Flagship and an Institutional scholarship at the same time - if qualified for both, only the higher one is awarded.

08_scholarships/college-of-business-entr.title: College of Business Entrance Scholarship (BSc Computational Finance and FinTech)
08_scholarships/college-of-business-entr.content:
College of Business Entrance Scholarship (BSc Computational Finance and FinTech)


                  
                  Short answer 
                  
                

JS1221’s business-side sibling, BSc Computational Finance and Financial Technology, has its own College of Business entrance scholarship: one-off HK40,000 with DSE Math/M1/M2/ICT/Economics/English >= 5* plus non-weighted JUPAS score >= 27.5, or HK20,000 at score >= 25 - on top of the university-wide tiers.


Question
Does the Computational Finance and FinTech programme (JS1221’s partner) have its own entrance scholarship?
Answer
Yes - the College of Business offers its own entrance scholarship for the BSc Computational Finance and Financial Technology major (the business half of the JS1221 double degree). Published tiers:

















CriteriaAmountDSE Math / M1 / M2 / ICT / Economics / English Language >= 5* and non-weighted JUPAS score >= 27.5HK$40,000 (one-off)Non-weighted JUPAS score >= 25HK$20,000 (one-off)
The sibling BBA Global Business (JS1001 - itself a flagship programme) has a parallel award with the same amounts, keyed to English / Chinese / Business, Accounting & Financial Studies / Economics >= 5* and the same score bands. The College notes that university-wide scholarships and financial aid beyond the CB entrance awards are also available for eligible students - so a JS1221 entrant can stack the Dean’s Tier 1 (HK$94,000/yr, since the CS+FinTech double degree is explicitly listed in the Dean’s table at 27.5/25) with the College’s one-off award.
Other unit-level awards exist for some departments (e.g. Department of Physics, Department of Materials Science and Engineering, Department of Electrical Engineering, Department of Accountancy), though no CS-department-specific entrance scholarship was listed on the university’s designated-unit list for 2025/26.
Examples

A JS1221 entrant with DSE Maths 5*, ICT 5* and a non-weighted score of 27.5 receives the Dean’s Tier 1 (HK94,000/yr) **plus** the one-off HK40,000 College of Business award - the two come from different award pools.
A plain JS1204 entrant is not eligible for the CB entrance scholarship - it is major-specific.

08_scholarships/dean's-scholarships-for-.title: Dean's Scholarships for JUPAS Entrants
08_scholarships/dean's-scholarships-for-.content:
Dean’s Scholarships for JUPAS Entrants


                  
                  Short answer 
                  
                

Local JUPAS entrants only. Tier 1 = HK94,000/yr at min scholarship score 27.5; Tier 2 = HK35,000/yr at 25. College of Computing (JS1204, JS1218, excl. ACT JS1070) uses these thresholds; JS1221 double degree also 27.5/25. Renewed yearly on CGPA; no application needed. Scale: 5**=8.5, 5*=7, 5=5.5, 4=4, 3=3; score = 3 core (excl. CSDDD) + 2 best electives.


Question
What are the Dean’s Scholarships and how do they apply to CS programmes?
Answer
Dean’s Scholarships are for local JUPAS entrants only and are awarded at the college/school level. Two tiers, both renewed annually on CGPA for 4-6 years depending on the programme:




















Tier 1Tier 2Value (per annum)HK$94,000HK$35,000Minimum HKDSE scholarship score (standard colleges)27.525
Thresholds by college/school (2027 entry): all standard colleges/schools - Biomedicine, Business, Computing, Engineering, Liberal Arts and Social Sciences, Science, Creative Media, Energy and Environment - use 27.5 / 25 for their non-flagship programmes. Exceptions: BVM (JS1801) has no Tier 1 and Tier 2 at 32.5; the double degree programmes have their own rows - BSc Computer Science + BSc Computational Finance and Financial Technology (JS1221): 27.5 / 25; LLB+BAcc, LLB+BSocSc (Crime Science) and BEng (ESE)+BBA Finance: 30.5 / 28.
The score uses the scholarship scoring scale (3 core subjects excluding ‘Citizenship and Social Development’ + 2 best electives; 5** = 8.5, 5* = 7, 5 = 5.5, 4 = 4…). No application is required; awards are notified by email on the JUPAS Main Round offer announcement date. A JUPAS entrant cannot hold a Dean’s scholarship together with a Flagship or Institutional scholarship - the highest applicable award applies.
Examples

Worked example (Tier 1): A student’s HKDSE results: Chinese 5, English 5, Maths 5, M1 5*, History 4, ICT 4. Scholarship-scale score = 3 core (5.5 + 5.5 + 5.5 = 16.5) + best 2 electives (M1 5* = 7, History 4 = 4) = 27.5 -> Dean’s **Tier 1: HK94,000/yr** x 4 years = HK376,000, which exceeds the ~HK$188,000 four-year tuition (full tuition and then some).
Worked example (Tier 2): English 5*, Maths 5, Chinese 5, M1 4, History 3, Geography 3. Score = core (7 + 5.5 + 5.5 = 18) + electives (M1 4, History 3) = 25 -> **Tier 2: HK35,000/yr** x 4 = HK140,000.
JS1221 double-degree entrant at 27.5: Tier 1 renewed for the full 5-year duration (up to 6) - one of the largest local award totals available - plus up to HK$40,000 one-off from the College of Business on top.
**JS1204 entrant at 27.5 with 4 subjects at 5** also clears the Institutional top tier (HK69,000/yr)** - they receive the **higher** award (Dean's Tier 1, HK94,000/yr); tiers are never stacked.

08_scholarships/diversity-grant-for-inte.title: Diversity Grant for International Students
08_scholarships/diversity-grant-for-inte.content:
Diversity Grant for International Students


                  
                  Short answer 
                  
                

All non-local students from underrepresented nationalities (except Top Scholarship recipients) get HK30,000 per year - HK120,000 over 4 years, or HK$90,000 over 3 years for Advanced Standing I entry - renewable, paid in installments, in return for annual volunteer activities.


Question
Is there a diversity grant for underrepresented-nationality students at CityUHK?
Answer
Yes. The Diversity Grant applies to all non-local students admitted from underrepresented nationalities, excluding Top Scholarship recipients. Terms:























Admission statusDurationAmount per annumTotal1st Year Entry4 yearsHK$30,000 (~USD 3,850)HK$120,000 (~USD 15,400)Advanced Standing I3 yearsHK$30,000HK$90,000 (~USD 11,500)
The grant is paid in installments and automatically renewed each year. Awardees are required to engage in a volunteer activity each year to enhance the internationalisation of CityUHK. It is in addition to the academic Entrance Scholarship Scheme (a student on the Half Tuition scholarship from an underrepresented nationality also receives the grant) - it is not an either/or choice.
Examples

A 4-year JS1204 student from an underrepresented nationality on the Half Tuition scholarship pays ~HK95,000/yr tuition but receives HK30,000/yr back via the Diversity Grant, netting ~HK$65,000/yr out of pocket - before any living costs.

08_scholarships/do-scholarships-change-w.filePath: 08_Scholarships/Do Scholarships Change Which CS Programme to Choose.md
08_scholarships/do-scholarships-change-w.title: Do Scholarships Change Which CS Programme to Choose
08_scholarships/do-scholarships-change-w.content:
Do Scholarships Change Which CS Programme to Choose


                  
                  Short answer 
                  
                

Often yes. At the same grades, ACT (JS1070) can pay 100% tuition + hall fees (Flagship, score 27.5+) while plain JS1204 tops out at Dean’s Tier 1 (HK94,000/yr); JS1221 gets Dean's tiers at 27.5/25 plus up to HK40,000 one-off from the College of Business. Scholarship value should be one input - not the only one - in choosing.


Question
Should I pick a CS programme at CityUHK partly based on its scholarship package?
Answer
This is a legitimate and common consideration, because the award pools genuinely differ by programme at identical grades. The 2027-entry picture for the three CS-relevant routes:

























RouteMax entrance award (local JUPAS)NotesJS1070 ACT (flagship)100% tuition + hall fees (score 27.5) or 50% (score 25); exchange up to HK$500,000; guaranteed hall berthFlagship Scholarships; not stackable with Institutional/Dean’sJS1204 BSc CSDean’s Tier 1 HK94,000/yr** (score 27.5) or Tier 2 HK35,000/yr (score 25); or Institutional up to HK$69,000/yr by 5 subject countHigher of the applicable tiers appliesJS1221 double degree**Dean’s Tier 1 HK94,000/yr** (27.5) / Tier 2 HK35,000/yr (25), up to 5-6 years plus up to HK$40,000 one-off College of Business awardLongest award duration of the three
A few cautions so the money doesn’t dominate the decision:

The Flagship full award is only reachable via ACT; JS1204/JS1218 candidates are capped at the Dean’s tiers even with perfect results.
Dean’s Tier 1 at HK94,000/yr for 4 years (~HK376,000) exceeds total local tuition (~HK$188,000), so at 27.5+ the JS1204 package is already effectively full-cost-plus.
The ACT vs JS1204 difference is also curriculum: ACT is the college’s globally oriented flagship track (exchanges, guaranteed PhD/PCL progression on meeting requirements) vs the established 4-year BSc with its five streams - weigh the programme fit, not just the bursary.
Non-JUPAS (IB/A-Level) candidates have the same structure with GCE/IB thresholds.

Bottom line: if your score is 25-27.4 and you are flexible, ACT’s Flagship half scholarship (50% tuition + hall fees) can be worth more than the JS1204 Dean’s Tier 2 (HK$35,000/yr); at 27.5+ both routes become near-full-cost, so choose on curriculum.
Examples

Student A (score 26): ACT half scholarship = 50% of ~HK47,000 tuition + hall fees free, 4 years; JS1204 Dean's Tier 2 = HK35,000/yr cash-equivalent. Both strong; ACT also guarantees the hall berth.
Student B (score 28): ACT full = zero tuition + zero hall fees; JS1204 Dean’s Tier 1 = HK$94,000/yr. Both effectively cover costs - curriculum decides.
Student C (score 24): ACT half not reached (needs 25); JS1204 Dean’s Tier 2 not reached either (needs 25); Institutional tier possible only with 2+ subjects at 5** and score >= 25. Below 25, neither route pays - the decision is purely academic.
