08_scholarships/entrance-scholarship-sch.title: Entrance Scholarship Scheme for International Students
08_scholarships/entrance-scholarship-sch.content:
Entrance Scholarship Scheme for International Students


                  
                  Short answer 
                  
                

For international (non-local) students in UGC-funded bachelor’s programmes: Top Scholarship HK$210,000/yr (tuition + university-managed accommodation + partial living expenses), Full Tuition, or Half Tuition - all renewable on CGPA, no application needed.


Question
Does CityUHK offer scholarships for international students applying to BSc Computer Science?
Answer
Yes. CityUHK’s Entrance Scholarship Scheme targets international students with excellent academic performance admitted to full-time government-funded bachelor’s degree programmes (JS1204/JS1218 included). Three tiers, awarded by merit with no separate application:





















TierCoverageTop Scholarship - HK$210,000 per year (~USD 27,000)Annual tuition + university-managed accommodation + partial living expenses (renewable)Full Tuition ScholarshipAnnual tuition fees (renewable)Half Tuition ScholarshipHalf of annual tuition fees (renewable)
Recipients must attain a minimum required CGPA each year to renew throughout their period of study. For context, the non-local tuition fee for 2026-27 entry is **HK190,000 per academic year**, so the Full Tuition tier effectively cancels the entire tuition cost; the Top tier adds accommodation (student residence ~HK20,800 per semester) plus a living allowance on top.
Note the BVM programme has separate, higher scholarship amounts - irrelevant to CS.
Examples

An international student admitted to JS1204 with top results on the Top Scholarship pays nothing toward tuition or university-managed hall and receives a living allowance for 4 years, conditional on maintaining the required CGPA.
At the Half Tuition tier, the student pays about HK95,000/yr out of the HK190,000 fee - a 50% reduction for the whole degree.

08_scholarships/flagship-scholarships-fo.title: Flagship Scholarships for JUPAS Entrants
08_scholarships/flagship-scholarships-fo.content:
Flagship Scholarships for JUPAS Entrants


                  
                  Short answer 
                  
                

Only for the ten flagship programmes (CS-relevant: ACT JS1070) - NOT for plain JS1204/JS1218. Full = 100% tuition + hall fees (double room) at min scholarship score 27.5; Half = 50% at 25. Plus exchange up to HK$500,000 one-off and a guaranteed hall berth. Scale: 5**=8.5, 5*=7, 5=5.5, 4=4, 3=3; score = 3 core (excl. CSDDD) + 2 best electives.


Question
What are Flagship Scholarships and does a regular BSc CS (JS1204) student qualify?
Answer
Flagship Scholarships go to local JUPAS entrants who register for one of the ten flagship programmes (Bio3 JS1300, BBA Global Business JS1001, ACT JS1070, PRIME JS1217, SAGE JS1120, GREAT JS1200, BVM JS1801, CREATE JS1040, INSPIRE JS1050, LLB JS1061). The flagship programmes share characteristics: globally oriented curriculum, overseas academic/research exchanges at top-ranked universities, internship/placement at prestigious institutions, and (where applicable) guaranteed admission to the respective PhD or PCL programme on meeting entrance requirements.
For CS applicants: ACT (JS1070) in the College of Computing is the only flagship programme relevant to computer science. A student admitted to plain JS1204 or JS1218 is not eligible for Flagship Scholarships and should look at the Institutional and Dean’s tiers instead.
Award value for the 2027 entry cycle (minimum HKDSE scholarship score - see Scholarship HKDSE Scoring Scale):

























ProgrammeFull (100% tuition + hall fees, double room)Half (50% tuition + hall fees, double room)Most flagships, including ACT (JS1070)27.525BVM (JS1801)3835LLB (JS1061)30.527.5
Flagship recipients also get exchange sponsorships of up to HK$500,000 (one-off) and a guaranteed berth in the halls of residence.
Examples

Worked example (full): Chinese 5, English 5, Maths 5, M1 5*, Chemistry 4, ICT 4 admitted to JS1070 ACT. Score = core (16.5) + electives (7 + 4) = 27.5 -> Full Flagship Scholarship: 100% tuition and hall fees (double room) for the whole programme + up to HK$500,000 one-off exchange sponsorship + guaranteed hall berth.
Worked example (half): the same profile with M1 at 5 instead of 5* scores 26.5 -> Half Scholarship: 50% tuition and 50% hall fees.
Thresholds differ by programme: most flagships (incl. ACT) 27.5/25; BVM JS1801 38/35; LLB JS1061 30.5/27.5.
Same 27.5 admitted to JS1204 instead: no Flagship (not a flagship programme) - the candidate falls to Dean’s Tier 1 (HK94,000/yr) instead. For a strong candidate choosing between ACT and JS1204, this is a real financial difference below 27.5 (ACT half = 50% tuition + free hall fees vs Dean's Tier 2 HK35,000/yr).

08_scholarships/flagship-scholarships-fo.title: Flagship Scholarships for Non-JUPAS Entrants (GCE A-Level and IB)
08_scholarships/flagship-scholarships-fo.content:
Flagship Scholarships for Non-JUPAS Entrants (GCE A-Level and IB)


                  
                  Short answer 
                  
                

Local non-JUPAS entrants (2027 entry) in the ten flagship programmes - including ACT (code 1070) - can get the Flagship full scholarship with GCE A-Level 4A* or IB Diploma >= 41 (half: 2A*+1A or IB 38-40), covering 100% (or 50%) tuition and hall fees (double room).


Question
Can a local IB or GCE A-Level student get a Flagship Scholarship into CityUHK CS (ACT) through non-JUPAS?
Answer
Yes. Local non-JUPAS entrants who register for one of the ten flagship programmes - including ACT (1070) via the College of Computing’s non-JUPAS route - are eligible for Flagship Scholarships on these 2027-entry criteria:




















AwardGCE A-LevelIB Diploma (incl. bonus points)Full Scholarship (100% tuition + hall fees, double room)4 A*>= 41Half Scholarship (50% tuition + hall fees, double room)2 A + 1 A*38-40
Plus exchange sponsorships up to HK$500,000 (one-off) and a guaranteed hall berth for Flagship recipients. Duration: 4-6 years depending on the programme’s normal duration; renewed on continuing in the flagship programme.
A-Level rules: two AS subjects count as one A-Level subject; the same subject cannot be counted at both AL and AS; GCE Chinese Language is not counted. No application is required - eligible students are notified by email in due course.
Examples

A local IB student admitted to ACT (1070) with a total Diploma score of 41 (including bonus points) receives the full Flagship Scholarship - 100% tuition and hall fees for the whole programme.
A local A-Level student admitted to ACT with 4A* + 2A gets the same full award; 2A* + 1A + … gets the half award. The same student admitted to JS1204 (1561A) instead would fall under the non-JUPAS Institutional Scholarship tiers instead.

08_scholarships/hksar-government-scholar.title: HKSAR Government Scholarship Fund for Non-Local Students
08_scholarships/hksar-government-scholar.content:
HKSAR Government Scholarship Fund for Non-Local Students


                  
                  Short answer 
                  
                

HKSAR Government Scholarship Fund scholarships support outstanding first-year non-local undergraduates, with targeted awards for students from Belt and Road countries/regions (e.g. Indonesia, Malaysia, Thailand, Myanmar, Mongolia) - full funding from the government, separate from CityUHK’s own schemes.


Question
Can a non-local student get a government (HKSAR) scholarship for CityUHK CS?
Answer
Yes, via the HKSAR Government Scholarship Fund - a government scheme (not a CityUHK one) that supports outstanding non-local students pursuing undergraduate studies in Hong Kong. Key points from CityUHK’s pages:

Aimed at first-year full-time UGC-funded programme students.
Targeted scholarships are made available to students from countries/regions along the Belt and Road, such as Indonesia, Malaysia, Thailand, Myanmar and Mongolia (other nationalities can also appear under the broader Fund, including ‘Belt & Road’ and non-academic-award/talent-development categories).
Awards are administered through the government fund with CityUHK handling nominations - check the current Fund guidelines on the HKSAR fund’s official site for amounts and eligibility, since the Fund’s rules are set by the government and updated per cycle.
Recipients appear alongside CityUHK’s own scholarships in department award lists (e.g. BMS 2025/26 lists HKSAR Government Scholarship and Belt & Road Scholarship recipients), so a CS student can realistically be on this list.

It is separate from and in addition to CityUHK’s own Entrance Scholarship Scheme - but government-fund rules may limit stacking, so confirm with both the Fund and the University for your nationality and year.
Examples

A first-year JS1204 student from Thailand may be considered for the targeted Belt & Road scholarship under the Fund in parallel with CityUHK’s Half Tuition entrance scholarship - the combination is confirmed through the University’s nomination process.

08_scholarships/how-to-apply-for-cityuhk.title: How to Apply for CityUHK Entrance Scholarships (No Application Needed)
08_scholarships/how-to-apply-for-cityuhk.content:
How to Apply for CityUHK Entrance Scholarships (No Application Needed)


                  
                  Short answer 
                  
                

You do not apply. Flagship, Institutional and Dean’s Scholarships are awarded automatically from your JUPAS application and HKDSE results; eligible students are notified by email on the JUPAS Main Round offer announcement date (4 August 2027).


Question
Do I need to submit a separate scholarship application when applying to CityUHK CS?
Answer
No. The official notes state: no application is required for Flagship, Institutional and Dean’s Scholarships. Eligibility is assessed automatically from your JUPAS registration (which programme you registered) and your HKDSE results, and eligible students are notified by email on the JUPAS Main Round Offers announcement date (per the JUPAS calendar - 4 August 2027 for the 2027 cycle).
Practical points:

Make sure your email address on JUPAS is current before mid-August - the award notice comes by email.
For non-JUPAS local entrants, the same no-application rule applies; eligible students are notified ‘in due course’.
If you are offered more than one scholarship, only the highest amount is awarded.
The schemes target newly admitted students; in special circumstances the University may consider re-admission candidates.
Questions: CityUHK scholarship details line +852 3442 8152 (admission matters: +852 3442 9094).

Examples

A student admitted to JS1204 on 4 August 2027 with three 5** subjects checks their email the same day and finds the Institutional Scholarship notification (HK$59,000/yr) attached to the offer.
No form, no interview, no separate form fee - the scholarship is decided from the data you already submitted to JUPAS.

08_scholarships/institutional-scholarshi.title: Institutional Scholarships for JUPAS Entrants
08_scholarships/institutional-scholarshi.content:
Institutional Scholarships for JUPAS Entrants


                  
                  Short answer 
                  
                

For local JUPAS entrants incl. JS1204/JS1218 (not flagships), per year: 4 subjects at 5** = HK69,000; 3 subjects at 5** = HK59,000; 2 subjects at 5** and scholarship score >= 25 = HK35,000; each tier also gives a one-off HK25,000 exchange scholarship. All 5** in one sitting; M1/M2 count (both = one subject). Scale: 5**=8.5, 5*=7, 5=5.5, 4=4, 3=3; score = 3 core (excl. CSDDD) + 2 best electives.


Question
How much is the Institutional Scholarship for a local JUPAS student admitted to BSc Computer Science or Cybersecurity?
Answer
Institutional Scholarships apply to local JUPAS entrants in any government-funded programme except the ten flagship programmes - so they cover JS1204 BSc Computer Science and JS1218 BSc Cybersecurity (and all other standard programmes). Tiers for 2027 entry, based on HKDSE results obtained in one sitting (repeat subjects do not count):

























CriteriaValue (per annum)Exchange scholarship4 subjects or more with 5** and Level 4 or above in either Chinese or EnglishHK$69,000HK$25,000 (one-off)3 subjects with 5** and Level 4 or above in either Chinese or EnglishHK$59,000HK$25,000 (one-off)2 subjects with 5**, Level 4+ in Chinese or English, and HKDSE scholarship score >= 25HK$35,000HK$25,000 (one-off)
Rules to know:

Category A subjects and Mathematics extended modules (M1/M2) count as the ‘5**’ subjects; if you took both M1 and M2 they count as one subject.
If English is used to count toward a ‘5**’, you must have Level 4 or above in Chinese (and vice versa).
The ‘score >= 25’ for the lowest tier uses the scholarship scoring scale (see Scholarship HKDSE Scoring Scale).
Duration: 4 to 6 years depending on the normal duration of the registered programme (JS1204/JS1218 = 4 years).
Renewed automatically each year on achieving the specified CGPA by the end of Semester B.
No application is required - eligible students are notified by email on the JUPAS Main Round offer announcement date.

Examples

Worked example (top tier): English 5**, Chinese 5**, Maths 5**, M1 5*, ICT 5, History 4, all in one sitting. Three subjects at 5** and Level 4+ in both languages -> **HK69,000/yr** x 4 = HK276,000 + one-off HK25,000 exchange scholarship (~HK301,000 total against ~HK$188,000 tuition).
Worked example (middle tier): English 5**, Maths 5**, M1 5*, ICT 5, Chinese 4, History 4. Two 5** subjects; score = core (4 + 8.5 + 8.5 = 21) + electives (7 + 5.5) = 33.5 >= 25 -> **HK35,000/yr** x 4 = HK140,000 + HK$25,000 one-off exchange.
English/Chinese cross-rule: if English is one of the 5** subjects used, Chinese must be Level 4 or above (and vice versa); otherwise that 5** does not count toward the tier.
M1/M2 rule: extended modules count as 5** subjects, but M1 + M2 together count as ONE subject. Repeated subjects are not counted; all results must be from one sitting.

08_scholarships/non-local-tuition-and-li.content:
Non-Local Tuition and Living Costs at CityUHK


                  
                  Short answer 
                  
                

Non-local (international) students pay about HK190,000 per academic year tuition (2026/27), a HK15,000 acceptance fee, and living costs of about HK$50,000-60,000/year - which is what the international entrance scholarships (Top/Full/Half tuition) offset.


Question
What does studying BSc CS at CityUHK actually cost an international student?
Answer
Official non-local figures for 2026/27 entry (admission fees-and-scholarships page):





























ItemAmountApplication feeHK$450 (up to 3 programme choices)Acceptance feeHK$15,000 (non-refundable, credited toward tuition)Tuition feeHK$190,000 per academic yearLiving costsHK$50,000-60,000 per academic yearAccommodationStudent residence: HK20,800 for two semesters; off-campus: HK50,000-60,000
So a four-year JS1204 degree without scholarship is roughly HK760,000 tuition + ~HK220,000 living before books and travel - and this is why the Entrance Scholarship Scheme (Top: HK210,000/yr covering tuition + university-managed accommodation + partial living expenses; Full Tuition; Half Tuition) is the headline decision factor for international applicants. The same acceptance fee is HK5,000 for local students, who pay about HK$47,000/yr tuition instead.
Examples

A Top Scholarship recipient’s four-year out-of-pocket cost drops to roughly living expenses not covered by the allowance - versus ~HK$980,000+ for an unaided international student.
The HK$15,000 acceptance fee is credited toward tuition on enrolment, so it is not purely ‘lost’ money.

08_scholarships/other-donor-scholarships.title: Other Donor Scholarships and Prizes at CityUHK
08_scholarships/other-donor-scholarships.content:
Other Donor Scholarships and Prizes at CityUHK


                  
                  Short answer 
                  
                

CityUHK offers 120+ donor-funded scholarships and prizes (e.g. HSBC Hong Kong Scholarship HK$50,000, Li Po Chun, Mapletree, AIA, Chi-Li Pao, Li Dak Sum Yip Yio Chin) for current students - separate from and stackable with the university-wide entrance scholarships.


Question
Besides the entrance scholarships, what other money can a CityUHK student earn during their degree?
Answer
Thanks to donor funding, CityUHK offers more than 120 scholarships, prizes and academic awards at undergraduate (and postgraduate) levels. Well-known ones visible in department award lists (e.g. Biomedical Sciences 2025/26) include:

HSBC Hong Kong Scholarship - funded by the Hongkong Bank Foundation for outstanding UGC-funded full-time local undergraduates (academic excellence + community involvement + communication); HK$50,000 per recipient.
Li Po Chun Charitable Trust Fund Scholarships (undergraduate), Mapletree Scholarships, AIA Scholarships, Chi-Li Pao Foundation Scholarships for Academic Outstanding Students, Li Dak Sum Yip Yio Chin Outstanding Student Scholarship, Ms Ada Chow Scholarships, Pao Ho Mei Chun Scholarships, CityU Scholarship / CityUHK Scholarship, Link University Scholarship, Lee Shau Kee Scholarships for Academic Outstanding Students.
Outstanding Athletes Entrance Scholarships for Local Students and the Residence Scholarship Scheme for Student Athletes for local athletes.
Student Development Scholarships, CMA and Donors Scholarships, and department-specific awards (the College of Business, for instance, adds its own entrance scholarships of HK$20,000-40,000 one-off for BSc Computational Finance and Financial Technology and BBA Global Business).

Most are for current students (i.e. applied for after admission, often via department/SDS nomination on academic merit) and are not subject to the ‘no concurrent awards’ rule that binds the Flagship/Institutional/Dean’s tiers - so a JS1204 Institutional Scholar recipient can still be an HSBC or Li Po Chun recipient in later years. The full list is maintained by Student Development Services.
Examples

A JS1204 student who received the Dean’s Tier 1 entrance award can be nominated for the HSBC Hong Kong Scholarship in Year 2 (HK$50,000, one of the most competitive donor awards) - the two awards coexist.
The College of Business entrance scholarship (HK$20,000-40,000 one-off) is an example of a unit-level award layered on top of the university-wide tiers for eligible majors.

08_scholarships/outstanding-athletes-ent.content:
Outstanding Athletes Entrance Scholarship for Non-Local Students


                  
                  Short answer 
                  
                

Outstanding non-local (international/continental-level) student athletes can get the Outstanding Athletes Entrance Scholarship - HK$200,000 per year covering tuition and partial living expenses - via the Student Athletes Admission Scheme (SAAS).


Question
Is there a scholarship route for international student athletes?
Answer
Yes. CityUHK’s Student Athletes Admission Scheme (SAAS) (run since 1997; 1,200+ student athletes admitted) provides admission and scholarships for outstanding non-local student athletes. The headline award is the Outstanding Athletes Entrance Scholarship (OAES) for Non-Local Students:

HK$200,000 per annum for athletes at International / Continental level - covering tuition and partial living expenses.
There are also athlete-entrance awards at lower competition levels and Residence Scholarship Scheme for Student Athletes components (hall place), with local student-athlete awards under the same umbrella.

Eligibility is set by competition level and the SAAS selection process; applications run through Student Development Services (SDS), with nomination forms on the CityUHK athletics page. This is a separate track from the academic Entrance Scholarship Scheme - a student who enters through SAAS gets the athletes’ awards rather than being stacked onto the academic Top/Full/Half tiers.
Examples

An international-level athlete admitted to JS1204 through SAAS with the OAES pays no tuition plus receives a living allowance of up to HK$200,000/yr - comparable in value to the academic Top Scholarship but with the entry route going through the athletes’ admission process.

08_scholarships/scholarship-hkdse-scorin.title: Scholarship HKDSE Scoring Scale (How Scholarship Scores Are Calculated)
08_scholarships/scholarship-hkdse-scorin.content:
Scholarship HKDSE Scoring Scale (How Scholarship Scores Are Calculated)


                  
                  Short answer 
                  
                

A different scale from JUPAS level points: 5** = 8.5, 5* = 7, 5 = 5.5, 4 = 4, 3 = 3, 2 = 2, 1 = 1. Score = 3 core subjects (excluding Citizenship and Social Development) + 2 best electives; best attempt used if repeated. E.g. 5** + 5 + 5 + 4 + 4 = 27.5.


Question
How is the ‘HKDSE score’ in the scholarship tables calculated, and is it the same as my JUPAS score?
Answer
It is not the same as the JUPAS admission score. Scholarship thresholds use CityU’s own scoring scale for HKDSE Category A core and elective subjects (including M1/M2):





































LevelScore5**8.55*755.544332211
The score adds 3 core subjects (excluding ‘Citizenship and Social Development’) + the 2 electives with the best results. If a subject was attempted more than once, the best result is used. Category C other-language subjects (Japanese, Korean, French/German/Spanish, Urdu) also have a scale (e.g. Japanese N1 = 7, Korean Level 6 = 7, French/German/Spanish C1 = 5.5) for use as electives.
Compare with the JUPAS level-point table (5** = 8, 5* = 7, 5 = 5, 4 = 4…) used for admission scores - the scholarship scale pays more for top grades (8.5 for 5**).
Examples

27.5 (Flagship full / Dean’s Tier 1 threshold): 5** + 5 + 5 + 4 + 4 = 8.5 + 5.5 + 5.5 + 4 + 4.
30.5 (LLB threshold): 5* + 5* + 5* + 5 + 4 = 7 + 7 + 7 + 5.5 + 4.
25 (Dean’s Tier 2 / Institutional entry): 5* + 5 + 5 + 4 + 3 = 7 + 5.5 + 5.5 + 4 + 3.
Category C language electives score on their own scale but map to the same values: Japanese N1 = 7, Korean Level 6 = 7, French/German/Spanish C1 = 5.5 - so a Japanese N1 elective counts the same as a 5* for the scholarship score.
Vs the JUPAS admission score: the same 5** + 5 + 5 + 4 + 4 profile is a JUPAS level-point score of 8 + 5 + 5 + 4 + 4 = 26 (weight 1) but a scholarship score of 27.5 - always recompute; never reuse the JUPAS number for a scholarship threshold.

08_scholarships/scholarship-renewal-and-.title: Scholarship Renewal and CGPA Requirements
08_scholarships/scholarship-renewal-and-.content:
Scholarship Renewal and CGPA Requirements


                  
                  Short answer 
                  
                

Institutional and Dean’s Scholarships renew automatically each year only if the student achieves a specified CGPA by the end of Semester B; Flagship Scholarships renew on continuing in the flagship programme. Non-local entrance scholarships also renew on CGPA. The exact CGPA figures are not published.


Question
What must a scholarship recipient do to keep the scholarship every year?
Answer
The renewals are automatic but conditional - no re-application, but the conditions must be met by the end of Semester B each year:

























ScholarshipAnnual renewal conditionInstitutional (JUPAS and non-JUPAS local)Achieve the specified CGPADean’sAchieve the specified CGPAFlagshipContinue studying in the flagship programme (i.e. do not transfer out of e.g. ACT)International Entrance Scheme (Top / Full / Half)Attain the minimum required CGPA each year throughout the period of study
CityU’s page does not publish the exact CGPA thresholds - it says ‘a specified Cumulative Grade Point Average’. In practice these operate as academic-progress conditions, so a serious drop in grades can end the award. Note CityU’s own undergraduate Dean’s List uses SGPA 3.7+ as the bar for outstanding standing, which gives a sense of the scale - but for your specific award, the CGPA requirement stated in your award letter governs.
Duration is also capped: awards run for the normal duration of the registered programme (4 years for JS1204/JS1218, up to 5-6 for longer programmes such as JS1221).
Examples

A JS1221 Dean’s Tier 1 recipient keeps HK$94,000/yr for up to the programme’s duration provided the CGPA condition is met by the end of each Semester B.
An ACT Flagship recipient who transfers out of the flagship programme loses the Flagship renewal from that point.

08_scholarships/scholarship-timeline-202.content:
Scholarship Timeline 2027 (JUPAS Entrants)


                  
                  Short answer 
                  
                

2027 cycle: HKDSE results 14 July; reprioritisation 14-16 July; JUPAS Main Round offers (and scholarship notifications by email) 4 August; enrolment mid-August; upgraded-results offers 19 August; Semester A starts 30 August.


Question
When exactly will a JUPAS applicant know whether they got a CityUHK scholarship in 2027?
Answer
Per the official ‘important dates for JUPAS entrants’ (2027, subject to changes), the scholarship decision arrives on the JUPAS Main Round offer announcement date: the same email that carries your programme offer states any Flagship / Institutional / Dean’s award, since no separate application exists.





































Date (2027)EventWed 14 JulyRelease of 2027 HKDSE resultsWed-Fri 14-16 JulyJUPAS programme-choice reprioritisationWed 4 AugustJUPAS Main Round offers announced - scholarship awards notified by email on this dateMid AugustEnrolmentLate AugustStudent orientationThu 19 AugustOffers for applicants with upgraded HKDSE results announced (an upgrade can change which scholarship tier applies)Mon 30 AugustSemester A 2027/28 starts
Strategy note: because scholarships are assigned from your results and your registered programme choices, reprioritising in mid-July (e.g. putting a flagship programme like ACT JS1070 ahead of JS1204) can change which award pool you fall into - Flagship tiers for JS1070 vs Institutional/Dean’s tiers for JS1204 - at no extra cost, since you don’t apply separately.
Contact for scholarship queries: +852 3442 8152 (admission matters: +852 3442 9094).
Examples

A student who reprioritises JS1070 above JS1204 on 15 July and is admitted to JS1070 with score 27.5 learns on 4 August that they hold the ACT Flagship full scholarship (100% tuition + hall fees), not the Institutional tier.
A student whose HKDSE results are upgraded after the main round gets a new offer (and possibly a different scholarship tier) on 19 August.

08_scholarships/what-do-flagship-scholar.title: What Do Flagship Scholarship Recipients Get (Benefits)
08_scholarships/what-do-flagship-scholar.content:
What Do Flagship Scholarship Recipients Get (Benefits)


                  
                  Short answer 
                  
                

Beyond the money: guaranteed hall berth, exchange sponsorships up to HK$500,000 (one-off), overseas exchanges, Global Work Attachment Programme, dedicated academic mentorship and early research engagement, Golden Key Club membership, and the Service Leadership Training Programme.


Question
What non-cash benefits come with a CityUHK scholarship?
Answer
CityUHK scholarship recipients (CityUHK Scholarships for Hong Kong Talents) receive a package of learning and advancement opportunities, on top of the tuition/hall-fee award:

Guaranteed berth in the halls of residence - for Flagship Scholarship recipients (not automatic for Institutional/Dean’s recipients).
Exchange sponsorships - up to HK500,000 one-off** for Flagship recipients; **HK25,000 one-off for Institutional recipients.
Global experience through overseas exchanges - outbound student exchange opportunities.
Global Work Attachment Programme (GWAP) - work-experience attachment with organisations abroad.
Academic mentorship - dedicated academic development and/or early engagement in academic research.
Golden Key Club membership - an all-round development platform and network for scholarship recipients.
Service Leadership Training Programme - service-learning platform for engaging with society.

These benefits matter for cost-of-living decisions: a Flagship recipient’s hall fees are covered (double room occupancy) and their hall place is guaranteed - relevant for students who would otherwise need off-campus accommodation (HK$50,000-60,000/year).
Examples

An ACT Flagship recipient in Year 1 gets a double hall berth at no cost (hall fees covered by the 100% award), a guaranteed place every year, and access to exchange sponsorship - a material saving versus a non-scholarship student paying ~HK$20,800+ for a student residence per semester.
An Institutional Scholar recipient (JS1204) gets the HK$25,000 one-off exchange scholarship but must secure a hall place through the normal residence allocation.

index.title: CityUHK CS Admission FAQ
index.content:
CityUHK CS Admission FAQ
A plain-language FAQ for City University of Hong Kong (CityUHK) — Department of Computer Science undergraduate admission: 400+ interlinked notes on the three majors, JUPAS scoring, published scores 2023–2026, the new 1.5× weighting policy, non-JUPAS routes, curriculum, programmes, internships, scholarships, and careers. Open the 🧮 What’s My Score? calculator to try your score live.
The three majors





























MajorSummaryIntake 2026/272026 scoreBSc Computer Science JS1204Flagship 4-year CS with 5 streams (AI, Cybersecurity, Data Science, Multimedia, Software Engineering), mandatory 9-month internship, HKIE-accredited~85 localmedian 23BSc Cybersecurity JS12184-year degree for the cybersecurity talent gap (System/Software Security, Cryptography, Privacy, Cyber Risk)~29 localmedian 20.5Double degrees JS1221 / JS10635-year CS + Computational Finance & FinTech / CS (AI) + Law — only ~10 places, JUPAS only~10–18 localmedian 23

Q1 — What makes these majors attractive?

Direct admission to the major — students join Computer Science or Cybersecurity directly, not a broad “department” where seats are re-allocated.
5 streams inside CS (AI / Cybersecurity / Data Science / Multimedia / Software Engineering) — one major, many specialisations.
Mandatory 9-month internship (Q2) — every graduate works before graduating.
97.5% full-time employment of BSc CS graduates (2024 survey); HKIE accreditation (first CS programme in HK).
Joint Bachelor’s with Columbia University (direct Year-1 admission from 2026/27).

Read: JS1204 BSc Computer Science Overview · JS1218 BSc Cybersecurity Overview · CS Study Streams Explained
Q2 — The mandatory internship: arrangement and why it matters

9 months in Year 3, credit-bearing, at real companies/government — after two full years of study.
Works 4 days a week with Fridays off for classes — the internship runs alongside study, it doesn’t pause the degree.
Jointly assessed by a CityU supervisor and the employer; a deliberate differentiator vs programmes where internships are optional.

Read: ITPP IT Professional Internship Overview · Why the Mandatory Internship Matters · ITPP Employers and Participating Companies
Q3 — Main courses and how they are arranged

4-year degree (~120 CU) in four layers: Gateway Education → College courses (programming from Year 1) → Calculus/Linear Algebra → CS core + electives.
Year 1 (33 CU) already includes programming (CS1302A), Computer Organisation, and computational probability modelling.
Students then specialise with 3 stream courses (or a mixed 5 electives).

Read: Curriculum of BSc Computer Science · CS Core Courses Explained · CS First Year Courses and Credits
Q4 — How is the JUPAS score calculated?

Best 5 DSE subjects (Category A, excluding CSD and Liberal Studies), all weight 1 in the published 2026 formula.
2026: median 23, lower quartile 22 (JS1204); Cybersecurity 20.5.
Minimum entrance: Eng 3, Chi 3, Math 3, CSD attained, plus Level 3 in one of ICT / Physics / Chemistry / Biology / M1 / M2 and a second Level-3 elective.
🧮 Try your score live in the What’s My Score? calculator — enter your DSE grades for the base score, the 1.5× version, and where you sit vs the medians.

Read: JS1204 2026 JUPAS Score Formula · Worked Example Computing JS1204 Admission Score · JUPAS Minimum Entrance Requirements for CS
Q5 — 🆕 NEW: the 1.5× subject-weighting policy

CityUHK is promoting a policy where English, Mathematics, ICT, M1, M2, Physics, Chemistry and Biology count at 1.5× level points — strongly rewarding the exact subjects a CS student takes.
Same profile, very different score under 1.5× (e.g. 5-5-5-4-4 in CS-relevant subjects: 24.5 → 36.75).
⚠️ The published 2026 formula is still best-5 weight 1 — always confirm the current year’s official formula before applying.

Read: 1.5x Subject Weighting Policy (Draft) Status · Subject Weightings in JUPAS Admission Scores
Q6 — How competitive is it? Which bands get in?

Most admitted students come from Band A (2026 median 23 ≈ 5-4-4-4-4+ profiles).
Around the lower quartile (22) is borderline (flexible admission may apply); Bands D and E normally have no chance.
Selection is score-first; bands are used as a tie-breaker.

Read: Typical Admission Competitiveness Most Admits Come From Band A · JUPAS Band Choices Explained · How CityUHK Ranks Tied JUPAS Candidates
Q7 — Is there a JUPAS interview?

No JUPAS interview is planned — selection is by admission score.
Competition achievements (OEA) and Principal’s Nominations exist but act as tie-breakers, not substitutes for the score.

Read: OEA and Principal’s Nominations for CityUHK CS · JUPAS Flexible Admission Arrangement Explained
Q8 — Non-JUPAS routes

Year 1 (both CS and Cyber): open to other qualifications including IB and GCE A-Level (codes 1561A / 1720A, HK$200 per programme).
ASI (Year 2) and ASII (Senior Year): for AD/HD holders — available for both CS and Cybersecurity in the coming year (normally a computing-related AD/HD, ~CGPA 3.0).

Read: Non-JUPAS Year 1 Admission · Advanced Standing I (Year 2) Admission · Advanced Standing II (Senior Year) Admission
Q9 — What about the double degrees?

5 years, two awards (CS + Computational Finance & FinTech, or CS (AI) + LLB).
DSE Mathematics level 4 required (JS1221); the LLB route needs English 5.
The final year is self-financed (credits beyond the 4-year/144-CU norm).
No local direct (non-JUPAS) admission — JUPAS only, and only ~10 places (JS1221) / 8 (JS1063).

Read: Double Degree Requirements and Structure · JS1221 Double Degree Overview · JS1063 LLB and BScCS Double Degree Overview
Q10 — Scholarships and cost

Local JUPAS entrants can be awarded Flagship / Institutional / Dean’s Scholarships (up to 100% tuition + hall, no application needed) — thresholds from ~25 (most flagships) to 27.5+.
The 🧮 score calculator shows where a student sits vs the medians.

Read: CityUHK Scholarship Overview · CityUHK Tuition Fees

🤖 Ask the AI — questions students keep asking
Some questions go beyond this site’s notes (job market, CS vs IT, AI and jobs). The AI chat (button at the bottom right of every page) answers them best-effort — site notes first, the web for the rest. Tap a question to copy it and send it to the AI:

9-month internship vs a summer internship: what are the benefits?
What is the CS / cybersecurity job market in Hong Kong right now?
Why should I choose Cybersecurity instead of Computer Science?
What is the difference between a CS major and an IT major?
Why should I major in CS but work in IT?
Will AI replace IT / software jobs?



                  
                  If the AI cites web sources, the answer is general knowledge — for CityU admission facts, the notes on this site are authoritative.

                  Before you apply 
                  
                

Published admission scores are reference points, not cut-offs — they describe where admitted students landed in past cycles and are not comparable across programmes or years. The 1.5× weighting policy is promoted by the CS admissions team but may or may not be reflected in the published formula for your entry year: always confirm the current year’s official formula on admission.cs.cityu.edu.hk. Every note states its source and its retrieved date — see Vault Freshness and Verification Status.
